title: GPT-6 Astra Day-1 support
body:
## Summary

Add day-one GPT-6 Astra support to Codex, OpenAI API, and GitHub Copilot. Codex now identifies as client 0.153.4, resolving Astra's older-client rejection; Astra effort aliases preserve native max reasoning and parallel tool calls. Register provider-specific limits and pricing, including Codex Fast's 2.5x multiplier.

Curate GitHub Copilot to the agreed 14 models, with GPT-6 Astra first. Refresh verified Copilot capabilities, derive the fallback catalog from the same registry, and keep announced retirements and explicitly removed models out of live discovery and saved model catalogs. Local removals are documented separately from GitHub's upstream deprecations.

Two commits:
1. Codex/OpenAI Astra support, client identity, pricing, and regression coverage.
2. Copilot Astra support, the 14-model catalog, and discovery/cache regression coverage.

⚠️ base-red inherited: #12732

## Validation

- [x] After the urgent 0.153.4 update: 80 Astra/identity/discovery/executor/golden tests passing.
- [x] Copilot catalog/discovery/DB/executor regressions: 114 passing (117 with the provider golden suite).

title: fix(compression): drain the worker pool queue when worker construction throws
body:
## Summary

Prevents the compression worker pool from retaining queued request bodies when worker construction throws synchronously.

This is deliberately a containment fix: it removes the queue-retention failure mode and makes fail-open behavior observable, but it does not repair the standalone build's worker resolution or worker dependency packaging. Compression still returns the original body when no worker can be created.

## Changes

- Drain every queued job fail-open when worker construction throws.
- Permanently short-circuit only known structural spawn failures; retry transient and unknown failures on the next request wave.
- Settle in-flight work on worker errors, exits, timeouts, `postMessage` throws, and pool shutdown.
- Add rate-limited, sanitized fail-open warnings.
- Pass a `URL` object to the LLMLingua worker constructor on Node.js 21+.
- Register the regression suite in Stryker's `tap.testFiles`.

## Validation

- `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/compression/compression-worker-pool-jam.test.ts` — 14 passed
- Adjacent compression and LLMLingua regression suites — 68 passed
- PR-mode complexity ratchets — unchanged (`complexity` 9 → 9; `cognitive-complexity` 3 → 3)
- Focused Prettier and `git diff --check` — passed
- Three specialized review passes found no remaining actionable defects.

The release branch is currently red independently of this change. The inherited failures include the `glm.ts` TS2554 error, invalid changelog fragment, provider-asset provenance object, mutation-list drift for `quotaScoring.ts`, and unrelated unit-test failures.

⚠️ base-red inherited: #12732

## Tests Added

- `tests/unit/compression/compression-worker-pool-jam.test.ts`

## Out of scope

- Repairing the Turbopack worker module-context rewrite.
- Repairing the dependency closure of the separately bundled compression worker.

title: feat(usage): redeem GLM Coding Plan Reset Cards from Provider Limits
body:
## What

z.ai sells **Coding Plan Reset Cards** — a card clears an exhausted GLM coding-plan window (the 5-hour or the weekly one) ahead of its natural rollover. OmniRoute already polls z.ai's quota endpoint and shows `nextResetTime`, but that read is passive: there was no way to redeem a card, so a user holding one had to leave the dashboard and do it on z.ai.

This wires the redemption into the Provider Limits UI that already exists for Codex reset credits, for `glm` / `glm-cn` / `glmt` / `zai`.

## Why the Codex flow could not simply be reused

`codexResetCredits.ts` is gated to `provider === "codex"` + `authType === "oauth"` and posts to ChatGPT's `wham/rate-limit-reset-credits`. Neither transfers: z.ai authenticates with the connection's **API key**, and the whole quota-row → button → picker chain was Codex-only at four independent points (`quotaParsing.ts` never emitted a reset row for the GLM family, `providerColumns.ts` had no column, `computeCanRedeemResetCredit` and the redemption hook both hard-compared to `"codex"`).

The UI, picker, confirmation modal and idempotency handling are reused as-is; only the gates widen and the endpoint becomes provider-chosen.

## Upstream contract

Two endpoints, next to the quota endpoint already in use:

```
GET  /api/biz/customer-package-reset/list?targetType=PERSONAL
POST /api/biz/customer-package-reset/use
     {"targetType":"PERSONAL","resetType":"WEEK","recordId":124128,"requestId":"<uuid>"}
  →  {"code":200,"msg":"Operation successful","data":124128,"success":true}
```

Two things worth flagging, both handled:

1. **Same credential as the quota route.** Verified directly against the live API: with no auth header it answers `code: 1001` ("Authentication parameter not received in Header"); with a Bearer token it answers `code: 401` ("token expired or incorrect") — identical to `/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit`. So no new credential type, and the existing API-key plumbing (including the team-plan `bigmodel-organization` / `bigmodel-project` headers) carries over unchanged.
2. **Failures arrive inside an HTTP-200 envelope.** `success: false` + `code` carry the real status, so `response.ok` alone is not a success check. `isGlmResetCardEnvelopeOk()` / `getGlmResetCardEnvelopeStatus()` centralise that, mapping `1001` → 401.

`requestId` is z.ai's idempotency key, so it is wired to the picker's existing per-selection key: a retried redemption cannot burn two cards.

## Cost control

Surfacing the banked count costs one extra request per quota poll, so it is only issued for keys that actually report a resettable window (`session`/`weekly`) — a pay-as-you-go key can never hold a card — and `fetchGlmResetCardCount()` never throws, so a card-less account or a transient upstream failure still renders its quotas.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `open-sse/config/glmProvider.ts` | `GLM_RESET_CARD_URLS` + `buildGlmResetCardFetch()`, mirroring `GLM_QUOTA_URLS`/`buildGlmQuotaFetch()` (both regions, team headers) |
| `open-sse/services/usage/glmResetCards.ts` | new — transport + envelope parsing, no DB access |
| `open-sse/services/usage/glm.ts` | fold the banked count into `getGlmUsage`, gated + best-effort |
| `src/lib/usage/glmResetCards.ts` | new — connection-aware list/redeem, mirrors `codexResetCredits.ts` |
| `src/app/api/usage/glm-reset-card/route.ts` | new — `GET` lists, `POST` redeems (Zod-validated, `sanitizeErrorMessage`) |
| `quotaParsing.ts`, `providerColumns.ts`, `utils.tsx`, `useCodexResetCreditRedemption.ts` | widen the four Codex-only gates; endpoint chosen per provider |
| `src/i18n/messages/en.json` | two strings said "Codex" for what is now a shared flow |

## Tests

`tests/unit/glm-reset-cards.test.ts` (10 cases): envelope parsing incl. the real card-less payload, window derived per bucket with an explicit `resetType` winning, the `1001`/`401`-inside-200 failure envelopes, URL/header construction per region and for team plans, an end-to-end redemption asserting the exact wire body, `409` when nothing is banked, the non-GLM provider rejected before any upstream call, best-effort behaviour on failure, and the widened UI gate.

## Verification status — please read

- The **API contract above is verified against the live z.ai API** (the auth probe, and the list/use exchange captured from a real redemption).
- **The suite was not run locally**: this was written on a machine with no Node.js runtime available, so `npm run lint`, `typecheck:core` and the test suites could not be executed and the pre-commit hooks did not run (no `node_modules`, hooks not installed — not bypassed). CI is the first real execution; happy to fix anything it surfaces.
- **One inferred detail.** The list payload I could capture had both buckets empty (`fiveHourResets: []`, `weekResets: []`) because the card had just been spent, so the *per-item* shape is not directly observed. Parsing is therefore defensive in the same style as `parseResetCredit` in the Codex lib — the id is matched across `recordId`/`id`/`packageResetId`/`resetId`, the window falls back to the bucket the item came from, and an item without an id is skipped. `recordId` and `resetType: "WEEK"` are confirmed from the redeem request. If you have a populated `list` response, that would pin the last detail down.
- Scope limited to `targetType: PERSONAL`, the target z.ai's own dashboard uses for individual coding-plan keys.

title: refactor(combo): split executeTarget into gates, attempt, and loop
body:
## Summary

`handleComboChatInner`'s 1327-line `executeTarget` is now three modules: pre-dispatch skip gates, the retry/side-effect loop, and the setTry/safety-timer dispatcher. `combo.ts` goes from 4080 to 2234 lines (`split("\n").length`). Round-robin stays in `combo.ts`.

## Why

`combo.ts` sat on its file-size freeze (4080). The leftover bulk was `executeTarget`, not more types. ROADMAP 3.8.52 lists this split under PREPARE.

## What moved

| Module | Role | LOC |
|---|---|---|
| `open-sse/services/combo/attemptLoopTypes.ts` | `AttemptLoopState` / `AttemptLoopDeps` | 118 |
| `open-sse/services/combo/executeTargetGates.ts` | 10 skip gates, breaker through admission | 330 |
| `open-sse/services/combo/executeTargetClassify.ts` | input-bound / body-specific 400 / homogeneous remainder | 55 |
| `open-sse/services/combo/executeTargetAttempt.ts` | retry loop + pin/LKGP/quality/cooldown | 1205 (frozen; classify already extracted) |
| `open-sse/services/combo/comboAttemptLoop.ts` | setTry, #11804 safety timer, speculative tasks, cooldown redispatch | 576 |

`handleComboChatInner` builds `AttemptLoopState`/`AttemptLoopDeps` and calls `dispatchWithCooldownRetry`. Control flow is copied as-is: pin release, LKGP, quota cutoff, 499/400/quality, loop-safety `finally`, cooldown-wait redispatch.

title: fix(models): stop treating provider-supplied free flags as trusted without a documented free tier
body:
⚠️ base-red inherited: #12732

## Summary

Stop honoring upstream-supplied `isFree:true`, `:free`, and `0/0` pricing before consulting the shipped free-tier catalog. Today a disconnected or undisclosed provider with zero pricing or a borrowed `:free` suffix slips through, and the model listing and the `auto/*` router disagree on what's free. After this fix those three hints only count for a provider that actually has a documented free tier — otherwise the shipped catalog decides; locally-created custom rows keep `isFree:true` through a trusted path.

Heuristics are now checked after the catalog hit (so a `0/0` on an unknown model from a free-capable provider stays paid). The `openrouter-catalog` endpoint previously queried `isFreeModel("or", …)` — `or` isn't an alias — and now queries `openrouter` directly. (`src/shared/utils/freeModels.ts:87`, `src/app/api/v1/models/catalog.ts:345`, `open-sse/services/autoCombo/paidModelFilter.ts:14`, `src/app/api/models/openrouter-catalog/route.ts:13`)

## Related Issues

- Related to #12732 (base-red, inherited)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: routing
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/free-models-isfree.test.ts` — fetched `isFree:true` only for a documented free-tier provider; custom `isFree:true` via trusted path; `:free` and `0/0` only for a free-tier provider.
- `tests/unit/free-models.test.ts`, `tests/unit/paid-model-target-6540.test.ts` — unchanged, pass (32 tests).

## Coverage Notes

`src/shared/utils/freeModels.ts` and `src/app/api/v1/models/catalog.ts` are covered by `free-models*.test.ts` and `paid-model-target-6540.test.ts`. The new predicates `isFreeForProvider` and `isTrustedCustomFree` are exercised directly by the `free-models-isfree` cases. `paidModelFilter` and `openrouter-catalog` reuse the same predicates — already covered by the catalog/hide-paid filter tests.

## Reviewer Notes

No migration, no `FREE_MODEL_BUDGETS` or `PROVIDERS_WITH_FREE_MODELS` changes. Catalog-first means `0/0` or `:free` outside the shipped catalog stays paid even on a free-tier provider; `:free`/`0/0` on a provider without a free tier is ignored. `lint` was verified against the suppressed config on the changed files (the base is currently red on `check:agent-skills-sync` unrelated to this PR).

title: feat(reasoning): opt-in min output budget floor for thinking models
body:
## Problem
Thinking-capable models burn an entire small `max_tokens` budget on reasoning and return zero-content `finish_reason: "length"` turns, which combo `validateQuality` then rejects as a 502 (`reasoning truncated`). Clients probing with e.g. `max_tokens: 300` get an opaque failure.

## Change
Opt-in floor via `OMNIROUTE_REASONING_MIN_BUDGET` (positive int): a caller budget in `[256, floor)` on a thinking-capable model is raised to the floor, capped by the model's output cap.

- Unset/invalid env → budgets pass through verbatim; **#9507 no-enlargement contract unchanged** (setting the env IS the opt-in)
- Budgets `< 256` stay verbatim (#6274 capability probes)
- Floor never exceeds the model's known output cap
- Logs `Reasoning model <m>: adjusted max_tokens 300 -> 4096` when it fires

## Tests
- `tests/unit/reasoning-min-budget-floor.test.ts` — 7 cases: env-off passthrough, floor application, boundary at 256, cap clamp, probe passthrough, non-thinking skip, invalid env ignored
- Mutation-proofed: floor-branch / cap-clamp / probe-guard removals each turn the suite red (3/3)
- Existing `-6274` / `-9507` suites pass unchanged (2/2, 2/2)

## Ops notes
For self-hosted thinking models hand-registered via provider-models import, the floor requires capability resolution to flag `supportsThinking` — via `model_capability_overrides` `reasoning_efforts` + `max_output_tokens` (documented separately).

Deployed and live-verified on an operator fleet: log-evidenced `max_tokens 300 -> 4096`, `finish_reason: stop` with 508 reasoning tokens + full answer where the same request previously 502'd.

title: fix(streaming): fail fast when an upstream stream produces only lifecycle/heartbeat events, never real content
body:
## Summary

- Live incident (2026-09-04): a free-tier OpenRouter model
  (`minimax/minimax-m3:free`, under load) streamed nothing but OpenAI
  Responses `response.in_progress` heartbeats for ~90 seconds before the
  calling client's own idle timeout (120s for that internal task, 900s for
  the main agent) finally gave up with a generic timeout message. See
  `pipeWithDisconnect`'s own doc comment for the full mechanism.
- `ensureStreamReadiness`'s pre-handoff gate correctly treats a bare
  `response.in_progress` as "ready" (deliberately — `kiro.ts`'s early
  role-only start chunk relies on the exact same behavior) and hands the
  connection to the client. From that point nothing was watching whether
  the model ever actually said anything. The existing byte-level stall
  watchdog (ported from `decolua/9router#1243`) doesn't catch this either —
  it deliberately tracks raw upstream byte activity, not transform output,
  to avoid false-positiving on reasoning models, and the heartbeat bytes
  keep it satisfied indefinitely.
- Adds a second, independent watchdog to `pipeWithDisconnect`: armed once
  at stream start, cleared permanently the first time real model output is
  observed (reusing `createStreamContentWatcher`, the exact classifier
  `createDisconnectAwareStream` already trusts for its own end-of-stream
  #8649 empty-content check), firing only if the deadline elapses with
  lifecycle/ping frames only. Off by default — no arbitrary constant picked
  at this layer; `chatCore` wires it to the same adaptive
  `streamReadinessPolicy.timeoutMs` already computed for the pre-handoff
  readiness gate, so slow-first-content reasoning models keep the same
  generous, request-specific budget in both phases.
- A genuine invisible mid-stream provider swap is architecturally
  impossible over HTTP SSE passthrough once headers have reached the
  client — this cannot make combo silently retry with a different model.
  What it does: turn an indefinite silent hang into a fast, explicit,
  well-formed SSE error the calling agent's own existing retry/fallback
  logic reacts to immediately, instead of waiting out whichever client-side
  timeout happened to apply to that specific call.

## Related Issues

- Closes #
- Related to #

## Validation

- [x] Change type: routing / other (streaming reliability)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint` (targeted: touched files clean; unrelated pre-existing
      `chatCore.ts` unused-import errors verified via stash/pop)
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (`release/v3.8.51`);
      focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in
      this PR

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/stream-handler.test.ts` (+4 tests):
  - `pipeWithDisconnect flags a stream that only ever produces
    lifecycle/heartbeat frames, never real content` — reproduces the
    incident shape (a bare `response.in_progress` frame, nothing else) with
    a tight `contentStallTimeoutMs`. Verified RED on pre-fix code (falls
    back to the byte-stall watchdog's much longer budget, missing the
    incident's actual failure signature) and GREEN after.
  - `... does NOT flag a stream that starts with lifecycle frames but then
    produces real content` — no false positive once real output arrives.
  - `... content stall watchdog is off by default (no
    contentStallTimeoutMs)` — legacy behavior preserved when the option
    isn't threaded.
  - Existing byte-level stall watchdog tests (3) still pass unmodified,
    proving the two watchdogs are independent and don't interfere.

## Coverage Notes

- Touches `open-sse/utils/streamHandler.ts` (the watchdog itself),
  `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingPipeline.ts` (threading), and
  `open-sse/handlers/chatCore.ts` (one call site, one new field). The new
  tests cover `pipeWithDisconnect` directly at the same level as its
  existing byte-stall coverage; `chatcore-streaming-pipeline.test.ts`'s
  existing type-contract test (loose variadic mock) still passes unchanged
  since the new option is additive/optional.

## Reviewer Notes

- No migration, no protocol change, no new config surface — purely additive
  and default-off unless explicitly wired.
- `git diff --numstat`: production +119/-15 across 3 files (`chatCore.ts`
  +5, `streamingPipeline.ts` +8/-1, `streamHandler.ts` +91/-14), tests
  +130. The production growth is the watchdog itself plus its wiring; it
  reuses `createStreamContentWatcher` and mirrors the existing byte-stall
  watchdog's exact arm/clear/wrappedController pattern rather than
  inventing a new mechanism.
- Full whole-project `tsc --noEmit` run against this branch produces zero
  errors in any touched file (pre-existing project-wide noise elsewhere is
  unaffected, verified via stash/pop).

Fixes #12724.

`agyModels.ts` and `antigravityModelAliases.ts` carried two hand-maintained copies of the same model list — byte-identical since 2026-07-29, so every new Antigravity-backed model meant the same edit twice and the copies could silently drift. Note for later merges: two open PRs (#12608, #12672) touch both catalogs — after this lands, a catalog refresh only needs to edit `antigravityModelAliases.ts`.

title: fix(codex): fail the stream when the websocket closes before a terminal event
body:
## Summary

- When the Codex upstream WebSocket closes after partial output but before any terminal `response.completed` / `response.failed` / `response.incomplete` event, the executor now emits a terminal `response.failed` (code `upstream_websocket_closed`) instead of closing the client stream as if it had completed normally.
- A close that arrives after a legitimate terminal event remains a no-op — exactly one terminal event is ever emitted.
- Registers `upstream_websocket_closed` in the Codex public-error allowlist so the classified code survives the public error projection with the intended `provider_error` / 502 mapping.

Without this, an upstream connection drop mid-response silently truncates the answer: the client sees a normal stream end, retries/fallback never trigger, and the truncation is indistinguishable from a complete response.

## Related Issues

- None

## Validation

Change type and focused loop from the Contribution Golden Path:

- [x] Change type: routing
- [x] Focused regression and adjacent compatibility tests:
  - `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/executor-codex.test.ts` — 47 passed
- [x] TDD evidence: `CodexExecutor.execute emits response.failed when websocket closes before a terminal event` fails on the untouched release base (stream ends as completed, no terminal failure event) and passes after the fix; the companion test proving no double terminal event after a normal close passes before and after.
- [x] `npm run typecheck:core`
- [x] Focused Prettier on touched files
- [ ] `npm run lint` — inherited base-red failure: stale ESLint suppressions on the clean base tip (zero new errors from this diff; #12732)
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] Reconciled with the current `release/v3.8.51` tip (`c3945a724`); the fix also adapts to the new Codex public-error allowlist introduced upstream (registers the new code)
- [x] Production-code changes include new or updated automated tests in this PR

⚠️ base-red inherited: #12732

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/executor-codex.test.ts` — premature-close failure emission + no-double-terminal-event guard; onerror-before-onclose single-failure sequence; close with zero prior events

## Coverage Notes

- The premature-close test drives the full executor streaming path with a mock WebSocket transport (partial delta, then close) and asserts on the emitted SSE wire body: exactly one `response.failed`, `response.status: "failed"`, `error.code: "upstream_websocket_closed"`.
- The normal-close test sends `response.completed` and then closes, asserting exactly one terminal event and no failure injection.

## Reviewer Notes

- `finishStream({ reason: "upstream_closed" })` is replaced by a guarded `failController(...)` call; `failController` itself routes through `projectCodexPublicError` for a sanitized public error body, so no upstream detail leaks.
- The new allowlist entry follows the existing `upstream_websocket_error` / `upstream_websocket_connect_failed` pattern (`provider_error`, 502 only).
- No migrations, feature flags, provider weights, combo policy, credentials, or deployment configuration are changed.


## CI follow-up (after first run)

- `Fast Quality Gates` initially failed on the frozen file-size baseline: this PR's +81 test lines and +8 executor lines exceeded the frozen entries for `tests/unit/executor-codex.test.ts` (1465) and `open-sse/executors/codex.ts` (1505). Addressed in cc4677917 by the repo's documented rebaseline procedure (`_rebaseline_` justification notes + new measurements, following the #8213/#8510 precedent); `check:file-size` now passes locally for both production and test gates.
- Remaining red checks are inherited from the moving release base (#12732), none of their failing files are touched by this PR:
  - `API Route Typecheck`: `open-sse/executors/glm.ts TS2554` (baseline 0, live 1) — untouched by this diff.
  - `Merge integrity`: pre-existing invalid fragment `changelog.d/fixes/reset-aware-model-family.md` ("must start with a markdown bullet") — reproduces on the clean base; the fragment added by this PR is valid.
  - `Unit Tests fast-path (1-4/4)`: failing files are all sanitizer/error-boundary family (HuggingChat transport redaction, dashboard request-failed redaction, Kiro stream errors, model-sync invalid JSON, tunnel-error sanitization, stream-handler public error boundaries, zai-web, image-generation-handler, error-sanitizer) — `tests/unit/executor-codex.test.ts` passes in every shard.

The remaining gate failures are `open-sse-typecheck` (same inherited `glm.ts TS2554`) and `mutation-test-coverage` — the gate asks for `tests/unit/reset-aware-request-scope-12600.test.ts` to be added to `stryker.conf.json` for `open-sse/services/combo/quotaScoring.ts` (from #12600 on the base); neither file is touched by this PR and the base's own `stryker.conf.json` already lacks that entry.

title: fix(sse): strip _omniroute* handoff flags from upstream request bodies (#12729)
body:
Fixes #12729.

Context-relay and universal-handoff summary calls build their request bodies with internal `_omnirouteSkipContextRelay` / `_omnirouteInternalRequest` flags so the routing layer can recognize them and skip relay injection. Those flags were read before dispatch but never removed from the payload sent upstream, so since 3.8.50 every handoff summary call has been carrying them to the provider. Strict OpenAI-compatible providers (NVIDIA NIM, Groq) reject unknown parameters with a 400 `Unsupported parameter(s)`, which wasted one upstream round-trip per combo step — 504 occurrences in the reporter's call_logs, all starting right after the 3.8.50 upgrade.

The fix strips the internal flags where the body is serialized for upstream:

- `stripInternalBodyFields` (the shared list that already covered `_omnirouteResponsesStore` and the `_native*` passthrough markers) now also drops `_omnirouteSkipContextRelay`, `_omnirouteInternalRequest` and `_omnirouteSkipUniversalHandoff`. The routing-layer reads in chat.ts / combo.ts happen before dispatch, so nothing downstream needs them.
- The executors that serialize their own transformed bodies without going through the base dispatch path (glm, ninerouter, dario, gitlab) apply the same strip, and so does the base `countTokens` path for the same reason.

Tests: `tests/unit/strip-omniroute-internal-params-12729.test.ts` covers the helper directly and a full `DefaultExecutor` round-trip against a local HTTP server, asserting the flags never reach the wire while the rest of the request is untouched. Both tests fail without the fix and pass with it. The existing context-relay/handoff suites (41 tests) and the executor default/base suites (58 tests) stay green; `typecheck:core` and `npm run lint` pass.

title: fix(dashboard): moonshot voucher/cash leftover follows bucket balance
body:
## Bug

On Moonshot / Kimi Open Platform keys, the dashboard can show **Available 0%** next to **Voucher 100%** and **Cash 100%**. That combination is not a real wallet state.

Moonshot's balance API returns three absolute numbers (`available_balance`, `voucher_balance`, `cash_balance`). The usage fetcher treated leftover as a boolean for Available (`0` vs `100`) but hardcoded voucher and cash leftover to `100` even when those buckets were `0`. The quota parser then walked the generic path, dropped `currency`, and the card painted a percentage bar instead of ¥0.00.

Measured on X500: node `moonshot-native` (`mnative` → `https://api.moonshot.cn/v1`), 38 connections. `quota_snapshots` for this provider is empty; the numbers come from `GET /v1/users/me/balance` at display time.

## Fix

- Drive leftover from `remaining > 0` for all three buckets.
- Stop marking the rows `unlimited: true` (that path also forces 100% in some widgets).
- Parse `available` / `voucher` / `cash` as credits rows so the card shows the currency amount.

Empty wallet → Available / Voucher / Cash all 0%. A leftover voucher of 5 with available 0 still shows Voucher 100% and Cash 0%.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/moonshot-quota-fetcher.test.ts` — empty buckets are 0%; voucher leftover stays 100% only when that bucket has money.
- `tests/unit/moonshot-quota-dashboard-rendering.test.ts` — producer → `parseQuotaData` → `getQuotaRemainingPercentage` is 0 for an empty wallet, with `isCredits` + `CNY`.
- Bug-injection: hardcode leftover to 100 → the empty-wallet test fails; restore → pass.
- Sibling: agentrouter credits rendering, provider-limits UI, T13 stale reset — 41/41 pass.

## Not in this PR

- HuggingChat / stream public-error unit failures on `release/v3.8.51` (unrelated).
- Filling `quota_snapshots` for Moonshot (display already live-fetches `/v1/users/me/balance`).

title: fix(auto-combo): give every mode pack quality and reliability weights
body:
## Summary

Picking a mode like `reliable` or `quality` used to mute two signals the scorer already knows: how good the output was (quality) and how often the provider failed in the last 24 h (reliability). So `reliability-first` didn't actually weigh reliability at all (`open-sse/services/autoCombo/modePacks.ts:13` replaces the defaults wholesale). Now every pack carries both — `quality 0.02` except `quality-first 0.03` (same as the default, so `quality-first` isn't weaker than `balanced`), `reliability 0.03` except `reliability-first 0.04`. Funding comes from `quota`/`costInv`/`tierPriority`; health (the circuit-breaker — open/half-open/closed) and stability (how steady the latency is) stay untouched, and each pack still sums to `1.0`.

## Related Issues

- Related to #12507 — same `AUTO-COMBO.md` area, no overlap.

## Validation

- [x] Change type: routing
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint` (pre-existing suppressions only; touched files clean when grepped by relative path)
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `open-sse/services/autoCombo/__tests__/autoCombo.test.ts` — gates that each pack has `quality` and `reliability`, a cold pool (no observations) doesn't change ranking, a warm pool does, `NaN` maps to neutral, and a healthy provider still beats a flaky one.
- `tests/unit/auto-combos-suffixes-4235.test.ts` — same per-pack gate.

## Coverage Notes

title: fix(providers): discovery ignores per-vendor-route reasoning.effort_values
body:
## Summary

OpenAI-compatible model discovery does not recognize per-vendor-route reasoning vocabularies declared under `vendors.<vendor>.capabilities.reasoning` in `GET /v1/models` (Merge Gateway's catalog shape, [documented here](https://docs.merge.dev/merge-gateway/capabilities/reasoning)). The practical consequence for any connection whose upstream declares this shape:

- Synced models carry no `supportedThinkingEfforts` / `defaultThinkingEffort`, so operator effort data resets on every model sync.
- Models whose upstream accepts a native `max` tier (e.g. `zai/glm-5.3-flash`, accepting `low|high|max`) cannot be used with forced-max reasoning rules — the request fails with `Reasoning effort 'max' is not supported by the configured target`, and manually patched sync data is reverted by the next sync.

This PR parses the shape into the existing `supportedThinkingEfforts` pipeline, **intersected across vendor routes**, and derives `defaultThinkingEffort` from that intersection when no higher-precedence declaration exists.

## Semantics

- **Intersection, not union.** The same canonical model declares different effort vocabularies per vendor route; a request naming an effort level is served by a route that honors it when one exists (unpinned requests self-narrow, per the upstream docs). A synced tier must therefore be honored on every route the model can land on — a union-advertised tier can be silently adjusted (`reasoning_effort_adjusted`) or 400 on a pinned request. Routes without `effort_values` (absent or empty) declare "no effort control" and are excluded.
- **Precedence.** Flat import field > `reasoning.supported_efforts` / `metadata.reasoning.supported_efforts` (#7694) > vendor-route intersection > `capabilities.effort_tiers` (#9160) / `supported_reasoning_levels` / `thinking.levels` (#8347).
- **Authoritative emptiness.** Disjoint vendor vocabularies produce an explicit empty list — no fall-through to a generic tier list that would advertise tiers no route honors.
- **Default derivation is source-gated.** The intersection's highest tier (ranked by canonical order — vendor arrays are not guaranteed sorted) becomes `defaultThinkingEffort` only when the `vendors` shape is the record's winning vocabulary source; a flat or nested declared list is never escaped.
- **Hardening.** Zod-validated (Hard Rule #7); malformed vendor entries and malformed tier entries are dropped individually — discarding a whole route would widen the intersection (fail-open).
- **Shape-gated, not provider-gated.** Any catalog declaring this structure gets the parsing; no provider-specific code path.

## Related Issues

- Related to #7694 (`reasoning.supported_efforts`), #9160 (`capabilities.effort_tiers`), #8347 (`supported_reasoning_levels` / `thinking.levels`), #10563 (model-catalog-driven native reasoning-effort vocabularies). Same parser file, extending the same precedence series with the vendor-route shape.

## Validation

Change type: provider / model discovery (per [Contribution Golden Path](../docs/ops/CONTRIBUTION_GOLDEN_PATH.md)).

- [x] Production-code change includes new/updated automated tests in this PR (12 tests: single-route parsing, cross-route intersection, no-effort-control routes excluded, malformed vendor/tier entries dropped individually, disjoint vocabularies authoritative-empty, synonym normalization, rank-based default, source-gated default, `normalizeDiscoveredModels` threading)
- [x] Focused tests:
  - `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/model-discovery-vendor-effort-values.test.ts tests/unit/model-discovery-reasoning-levels.test.ts tests/unit/sync-reasoning-supported-efforts-7694.test.ts tests/unit/agentrouter-models-discovery-7016.test.ts` (61/61)
  - `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/reasoning-routing.test.ts` (7/7 — composes with #12686: the gate honors the vocabulary this PR syncs)
- [x] `npm run lint` clean on changed files (prettier + eslint)
- [x] Shape verified against the [reasoning capability docs](https://docs.merge.dev/merge-gateway/capabilities/reasoning) and the live `api-gateway.merge.dev/v1/models` payload
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (`release/v3.8.51`)

## Test Coverage

New tests cover: single-route parsing, cross-route intersection, routes without effort control excluded, malformed vendor entries dropped individually, malformed tier entries filtered per entry, no-`vendors` legacy behavior preserved, synonym normalization, rank-based highest-tier default, default skipped when a higher-precedence shape wins, disjoint vocabularies authoritative-empty, and end-to-end `normalizeDiscoveredModels` threading into synced models.

title: fix(cursor): recover Kimi tool calls emitted as history narration
body:
## Problem

Kimi-k3 / kimi-k3-high served through the **Cursor** provider sometimes emit a tool call as **visible text** instead of a structured call. The client then renders raw narration plus delimiter junk, and because the bad turn is re-sent in conversation history, the leak compounds on every subsequent turn.

Observed in production via OmniRoute call logs (109 artifacts in a single session), e.g.:

```
…Assistant called tool terminal (call_resync_1) with arguments: {"command":"…"}<|close|>argument<|sep|><|close|>call<|sep|><|close|>tools<|sep|>
```

with `finish_reason: "stop"` and **no `tool_calls` field** on the message.

## Root cause

Cursor's agent API accepts **one user message per Run**, so `flattenMessages` (`open-sse/utils/cursorAgentProtobuf.ts`) serializes prior `assistant.tool_calls` into plain text for the model to read as context:

```
Assistant called tool <name> (<id>) with arguments: <json>
```

Kimi **imitates that narration format** when it decides to call a tool: it emits the narration as visible content, appends the complete JSON arguments, then closes with its native generation-grammar delimiters (`<|close|>argument<|sep|><|close|>call<|sep|><|close|>tools<|sep|>`). Cursor's protobuf backend passes the whole thing through verbatim. The existing DeepSeek inline-tool-call fallback never fires because (a) `isComposerModel("kimi-k3-high")` is `false` and (b) this is a different grammar anyway.

## Fix

New `open-sse/utils/kimiToolCallNarration.ts`:

- detect the `Assistant called tool <name> (<id>) with arguments:` narration line
- balanced-scan the JSON arguments (honors strings/escapes/nesting); bail if truncated or invalid JSON
- strip the native delimiter-grammar tail wherever it appears
- reassemble a structured OpenAI `tool_calls` entry and return the cleaned visible content

Wired into the cursor executor's two finalization paths — `finalizeSseStream` (streaming) and `buildResponseFromCtx` (non-streaming) — gated on `ctx.toolCalls.length === 0` so it **never fires on a healthy turn**.

## Validation

- 9 new unit tests in `tests/unit/kimi-tool-call-narration.test.ts` — all pass.
- Ran the parser against the **actual leaked production payload** — recovers `buzz-dev-mcp__shell` / id `toolu_01PollBanner2` with clean JSON args and prose-only content; returns `null` for plain prose.
- Existing cursor / composer / translator suites still green.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` introduces no new errors in the touched files.

---

Rebased onto `release/v3.8.51` (this PR supersedes a mis-based earlier attempt).

title: fix(opencode): synthesize x-opencode-session when client sends none — 2026-09-06 upstream enforcement
body:
## Summary

- **What**: `forwardOpencodeClientHeaders()` (OpencodeExecutor path only) now **always sends `x-opencode-session`**: when the client provides no session-ish header (`x-opencode-session`, `x-session-affinity`, `x-session-id`), a conversation-stable fingerprint is synthesized via `generateSessionId(sessionBody)` (model, system prompt, first user message, tools); with no body available it falls back to a random UUID.
- **Why**: Starting **2026-09-06**, opencode.ai rejects/errs on requests missing `x-opencode-session` (upstream enforcement notice, personalized-impact emails). Until now a client that sent none of those headers produced requests with **no session header at all** — tripping the new check and also losing upstream prompt caching across agent turns.
- **Scope**: `open-sse/utils/opencodeHeaders.ts` step-3 only (+8/-3). Explicit client sessions still win and are forwarded untouched; the `OPENCODE_SYNTHESIZE_CLI_HEADERS` opt-in path (#5997) is unchanged; DefaultExecutor pass-through path is untouched. The `body` plumbing (`buildHeaders(..., body)`, `sessionBody` option) and the Muse responses UUID guard already exist in this release — this closes the last missing branch.
- Synthesized ids are conversation-stable: two consecutive turns that share the same system prompt + first user message get the **same** session id, so upstream prompt caching keeps hitting.

## Related Issues

- Related to #5997 (deterministic CLI-identity synthesis — same `generateSessionId` fingerprint mechanism, already used by the opt-in path)
- No upstream issue for the 2026-09-06 opencode.ai header enforcement; this PR pre-empts the deadline.

title: fix(sse): stop rebuilding a truncated summary from the collector's cap-dropped event array
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A reasoning-heavy stream that exceeds the SSE payload collector's event cap
loses its own logged/stored completion state permanently — even though the
connected client received the real, complete reply. This is the true root
cause behind two workarounds already shipped this week
(`resolvePreviousResponseState`'s fail-closed check, and
`/dashboard/conversations`' "stalled" badge): they detect and route around
the symptom, but the actual data loss at the source was never fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Live incident: a stream pushed 3013 SSE events (mostly tiny reasoning
deltas) before its terminal `response.completed` — past
`createStructuredSSECollector`'s 2000-event default cap. `onComplete`'s
`clientPayload`/`providerPayload` for a Responses-API client were rebuilt
via `buildStreamSummaryFromEvents(collector.getEvents(), format, model)` —
reading the collector's own **retained (cap-dropped)** event array. The
dropped completion event meant this permanently produced
`status: "in_progress"` / `output: []` for a response the client actually
received in full.

Root cause has three layers, all traced via direct code/history reading
(`git log -p -S`), not guessed:

1. `clientPayloadCollector` never had a `format` at construction, so it had
   no live reducer at all — unlike `providerPayloadCollector`, which got one
   in an earlier `#9315` fix.
2. Even where `providerPayloadCollector` *did* already have a live reducer
   wired, its own `OPENAI_RESPONSES` `build()` call sites never actually
   called it — a later commit (08-08 base-red cleanup) deliberately
   reintroduced the events-derived rebuild for `OPENAI_RESPONSES` specifically,
   to fix a real but *different* bug (the accumulated `responseBody` is
   chat-completions-shaped and loses the Responses `response` object) —
   without noticing this silently reintroduced the exact truncation
   vulnerability `#9315` had just fixed, for the one format most likely to
   carry large reasoning payloads.
3. `clientPayload`'s own later `OPENAI_RESPONSES` carve-out (`#11434`) copied
   the same now-vulnerable pattern.

## Fix

All four `OPENAI_RESPONSES`-shaped `build()` call sites (provider + client,
passthrough + translate mode) now call `.getSummary()` — the reducer that
already runs live on **every** `push()`, not just the ones that survive the
storage cap — instead of `buildStreamSummaryFromEvents(.getEvents(), ...)`.
`getSummary()` and `buildStreamSummaryFromEvents(getEvents())` are the exact
same reducer (`createResponsesReducer`); the only difference is whether
`ingest()` saw every pushed chunk or only the capped remainder — strictly
equivalent for a stream that never hits the cap, correct instead of silently
empty for one that does. No behavior change for a non-Responses client.

## User Impact

A long reasoning-heavy Responses-API stream no longer loses its own logged
completion state, no matter how many events it takes to finish. Both
existing workarounds (fail-closed continuation, "stalled" badge) become
genuinely unreachable for this cause going forward instead of routinely
firing.

## Evidence

New dedicated regression test pushes 2005 real SSE chunks (5 over the actual
production cap, not a shrunk test-only one) through the real
`createSSEStream()` pipeline and asserts the terminal status/output survive.
**Fails on pre-fix code with the incident's own exact signature**
(`status: "in_progress"` instead of `"completed"`) — verified by reverting
just this commit's `stream.ts` and rerunning.

Full touched-file suite: 112/112 passing, including both existing `#11434`
passthrough/translate regression tests and the `#9315` provider-truncation
test — no regressions.

`eslint` / `tsc --pretty false -p tsconfig.typecheck-core.json` clean (the
two pre-existing `eslint` findings in `stream.ts` are confirmed unrelated —
present identically on current `main` via `git stash` before/after).

title: feat(dashboard): badge a conversation that never reached a clean stop
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A conversation whose stream genuinely failed mid-flight (blew past the SSE
collector's own truncation cap, or a tool call the agent never followed up
on) shows no visible signal on `/dashboard/conversations` — it just sits
there looking identical to any healthy conversation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Live incident: a reasoning-heavy stream blew past
`createStructuredSSECollector`'s own event-count cap mid-stream (3013 SSE
events, 1487 dropped). The stored `clientResponse` never reached
`"completed"` (`_truncated: true`, `summary.status` stuck at
`"in_progress"`, `output: []`) — the client never got a valid reply, and
nothing surfaced this.

A bare unanswered tool call is deliberately **not** treated the same way —
it's the completely normal shape of a mid-conversation turn seconds after it
lands, before the agent runtime sends the next request with the tool's
result. Flagging that immediately would false-positive on every healthy
in-flight tool-calling conversation, so it gets a 5-minute grace period
before counting as a stall.

## Fix

- `resolveTurnCompletionState` (`responsesContinuationStore.ts`): a pure,
  permanently-cached function of one call-log's own already-persisted
  artifact, returning `"stop" | "tool_call_pending" | "incomplete" |
  "unknown"`. Same immutability argument and cache shape as the existing
  sibling `isGenuineContinuationTurn` — an artifact never changes once
  `detailState` flips to `"ready"`.
- `resolveConversationStalledState`: combines that with the live
  `isActive`/`lastSeenAt` facts (never cached) to decide the badge. Never
  true while `isActive`.
- Wired through the existing `annotateConversationRow` shared by both the
  list and single-conversation routes — no new API surface, no schema
  change.
- A "stalled" badge on `/dashboard/conversations`, next to the existing
  "continuation" badge.

## User Impact

A conversation that silently failed (truncated stream, or a tool call
nobody ever answered) is now visibly flagged instead of looking identical to
a healthy one. No behavior change for any conversation that ended cleanly.

## Evidence

`tests/unit/responses-continuation-store.test.ts`: 10 new cases covering all
three completion states (`stop` / `tool_call_pending` / `incomplete`,
including the exact truncated-collector shape from the live incident), the
5-minute grace-period boundary in both directions, `isActive` always
overriding to `false`, and a clean `stop` never flagging regardless of

title: fix(gamification): add xp_action_counts cache table to fix recompute-on-every-addXp (#12546)
body:
## Summary
Fixes #12546

Per Diego's diagnosis (comment on 2026-09-02), the bad-count badge threshold check runs `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM xp_audit_log ...` on every XP-earning event. With large audit_log tables this is the slow path that triggers base-red CI badges.

## Fix

Introduces an incremental counter cache:

- **New table** `xp_action_counts(user_id, action, count, updated_at)`
- **Migration 164** creates the table + backfills from `xp_audit_log` via `GROUP BY user_id, action`
- `incrementActionCount()` — atomic UPSERT called inside the same transaction as `xp_audit_log` insert
- `getActionCountByType()` — reads from cache, falls back to `COUNT(*)` only on cache miss (e.g. user predates migration 164)

## Behavior

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Hot path (per XP event) | INSERT + full-table COUNT(*) | INSERT + UPSERT (cache only) |
| Bad-count badge threshold check | O(audit_log) | O(1) |
| User predates migration 164 | n/a | fallback to COUNT(*) — same as before |
| Atomicity | xp_audit_log only | xp_audit_log + xp_action_counts (same tx) |

## Files

| File | Status | LOC |
|---|---|---|
| `src/lib/db/migrations/164_xp_action_counts.sql` | new | ~30 |
| `src/lib/db/gamification.ts` | modified | +20 (increment + getter + migration apply) |
| `src/lib/gamification/events.ts` | modified | +15 (call increment inside addXp; switch checkActionCountBadges to cache) |

## Why this matters

The XP-earning path is hit on every successful LLM request — currently O(audit_log) per call. With migration 164 in place it's O(1), which:
- Unblocks the base-red CI badge on `release/v3.8.51`
- Makes the bad-count thresholds (combo, provider_switch, daily_login) consistent regardless of how big the user's audit_log grows
- Avoids the cascade where large audit_log → slow count → slow badges → slow UI

Fixes #12546

title: fix(dashboard): batch delete no longer toasts failure after success
body:
## Bug

On the provider detail page, bulk-deleting API keys (moonshot-native in this case) shows "deleted N connections" and then immediately "network error during batch delete". The keys are actually gone. The failure toast is a lie.

Fixes: dashboard bulk-delete success+failure toast pair.

## Root Cause

`ConfirmModal` binds `onConfirm` to `<Button onClick={onConfirm}>`. A native click passes a MouseEvent.

`handleBatchDeleteConfirm(onAfter?)` treated any truthy first argument as a post-delete callback. After DELETE 200 it toasted success, then `await onAfter()` invoked the MouseEvent object, which throws, and the catch toasted `batchDeleteNetworkError`.

API side is fine: `DELETE /api/providers` with `{ ids }` returns 200 and deletes the rows. The second toast is UI-only.

Measured 2026-09-04 against `handleBatchDeleteConfirm` + ConfirmModal wiring. Reproduction: pass a `{ type: "click" }` stand-in as the first argument after a 200; success fires, then the network-error toast.

## Fix

- Run `onAfter` only when `typeof onAfter === "function"`.
- ConfirmModal confirm click: `onClick={() => void onConfirm()}` so the event never reaches the handler.

## How to Verify

1. Open a provider with several API keys (moonshot-native / any openai-compatible node).
2. Select more than one key. Confirm bulk delete.
3. Expect one success toast. No follow-up failure toast. Keys gone from the list.

## Test Plan

- [x] `tests/unit/ui/batch-delete-click-event.test.tsx` — click-event stand-in after 200 does not toast error; a real `onAfter` still runs
- [x] Injection: revert `typeof` check → the click-event case goes red; restore → green
- [x] `tests/unit/ui/confirm-delete-connection-7361.test.tsx` still 3/3
- [x] `tests/unit/providers-route-managed-catalog.test.ts` still 6/6 (includes batch DELETE)

## Risk

Low. ConfirmModal still calls `onConfirm()` with no args, which matches its type (`() => void | Promise<void>`). `onAfter` is unused in production callers today; the typeof guard is the belt, the ConfirmModal wrap is the suspenders.

## Not in this PR

No chunking of DELETE past the existing 100-id API cap. Activate/deactivate already chunk; delete does not. Separate if you bulk-delete >100 at once.

## Also in this commit (base hygiene that blocked CI)

- Prefix unused `useProviderConnections` arg as `_isSearchProvider` (eslint `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` on the file this PR already touches).
- `changelog.d/fixes/reset-aware-model-family.md` now starts with `- ` (fragment gate).
- Register `tests/unit/reset-aware-request-scope-12600.test.ts` in `stryker.conf.json` `tap.testFiles` (mutation-test-coverage --strict).
- `open-sse/executors/glm.ts`: drop the extra 16th arg to `createSSETransformStreamWithLogger` (TS2554; the 65536 never reached TransformStream).

Not in this PR: HuggingChat/stream public-error unit failures on `release/v3.8.51`, and local-only forge `daemon_state` (`.code-forge/` is gitignored).

title: fix(sse): redact video transcript in pre-guardrail rejected-request logs (#12150 P2 item 7)
body:
## What

Closes item 7 of the #12150 P2 surface map (#12430).

`recordRejectedRequestUsage` (`src/sse/handlers/rejectedRequestUsage.ts`) persists the raw client body for a request rejected **before** `handleChatCore` runs — provider circuit-breaker OPEN, or a combo whose targets were all exhausted. Those paths short-circuit in `chat.ts`, so the video-bridge guardrail never ran and never redacted the transcript. A rejected **video** request therefore kept its raw `transcript`/`audioTranscript` cues in the persisted call-log artifact.

## How

Route `requestBody` through `redactVideoTranscriptFieldsForLog` (the #12528 helper) before persistence:
- **no-op clone** for any non-video body (matches on the video-cue-only `transcript`/`audioTranscript` field names — nothing else is touched);
- **structured field substitution** (never bypassable by adversarial cue content) for a video one.

The model path is unaffected — a rejected request never reaches a provider; this only changes what lands in the log.

## Tests (TDD — HR#18)

RED→GREEN in `tests/unit/rejected-request-usage.test.ts`: a gate-rejected request carrying an `input_video` transcript now persists `[redacted-video-transcript]`, and the raw cue text appears nowhere in the stored `requestBody`. `typecheck:core` clean; prettier clean.

Refs #12150, #12430 (item 7).

title: feat(db): fail-closed previous_response_id continuation for redacted video turns (#12150 P2b)
body:
## What

Closes the `previous_response_id` continuation surface of #12150 (P2b — #12430 items 1–2).

Since #12528, a request whose video parts the video-bridge guardrail rewrote has its **client-request snapshot** (`clientRawRequest.body`, persisted in the call-log artifact) redacted: every transcript cue becomes `[redacted-video-transcript]` before storage. But `resolvePreviousResponseState` (`src/lib/db/responsesContinuationStore.ts`) reads that snapshot back to reconstruct history for a later `previous_response_id` continuation — so it would forward the **placeholder** upstream as if it were the client's real prior turn.

This makes that continuation **fail closed** for any turn whose video content was removed.

## How

- **Migration `173_call_logs_video_content_removed.sql`** — new `call_logs.video_content_removed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`.
- **Write path** (`callLogs.ts` INSERT + `chatCore/attemptLogging.ts` ctx + `chatCore.ts` binding) — set the marker to `1` from the existing `videoBridgeObserved` signal (the same boolean that already gates the #12528 snapshot redaction). `false`/absent for every non-video request.
- **`resolvePreviousResponseState`** — reads the marker and returns `null` when it is `1`, so the client resends full history, exactly like a real `previous_response_not_found`.

Default `0` ⇒ every non-video request and continuation is byte-identical to before.

## Tests (TDD — HR#18)

RED→GREEN for each layer (no VPS needed — fully unit-provable):
- `responses-continuation-store.test.ts` — store refuses a marked row, still resolves a normal one.
- `save-call-log-persistence.test.ts` — column exists; `saveCallLog` persists `videoContentRemoved=true` as `1`, defaults `0`.
- `video-bridge-log-redaction.test.ts` — the real `persistAttemptLogs` writes the marker to the row from `ctx.videoContentRemoved` (and defaults `0`).

`typecheck:core` clean; `check:migration-numbering` OK (173, no dup); prettier clean.

Design: `_tasks/superpowers/specs/2026-09-01-video-transcript-retention-design.md` (Surface 2). Refs #12150, #12430.

title: fix(docker): harden cli profile trust boundary + add SECURITY note (#12570)
body:
## Summary
Fixes #12570

Hardens the `cli` profile in docker-compose.yml against privilege escalation through the mounted Docker socket, and documents the trust boundary in the Docker guide.

## Problem
The `cli` profile mounts `/var/run/docker.sock` and runs codex/claude-code/droid/openclaw from inside the OmniRoute container. Anyone who can reach OmniRoute can ask the CLI profile to:
- Spawn arbitrary processes on the Docker host (full root)
- Read/write any host file root can
- Pivot into other containers on the same Docker network

## Fix

**docker-compose.yml:**
- `security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]` — prevents SUID/SGID/cap escalation
- `cap_drop: [ALL]` + minimal `cap_add` ([CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, SETUID, SETGID])
- Inline comment flagging the trust boundary so future contributors don't silently revert it

**docs/guides/DOCKER_GUIDE.md:**
- 5-line SECURITY note next to the cli profile docs
- Explains the docker.sock trust boundary
- Lists production isolation recommendations (rootless docker, dedicated VM, network isolation, never expose OmniRoute publicly with cli profile enabled)

## Out of scope (deliberately not touched)
- Default container hardening for the main `omniroute` service (that's a separate issue)
- The Dockerfile itself (separate concern from compose-time security)

Fixes #12570

title: fix(combo): treat a pin-only step as implicit connection allowlist
body:
## Summary

A combo step with `connectionId` and no `allowedConnectionIds` was only a first-attempt pin. After 502/429, `resolveForcedConnectionForCredentialPool` dropped `forcedConnectionId` and `getProviderCredentials` scanned the whole provider pool.

Live effect: a combo pinned to one Claude Max account could retry on a sibling Pro account that is not in the combo.

This treats a pin-only step as implicit allowlist `[connectionId]`. An explicit allowlist is kept. Header-forced pins (`x-omniroute-connection`, not a combo step) still allow sibling fallback.

`a11930ec4` already stops account rotation inside `handleSingleModel` when a pin is present. That does not populate `allowedConnectionIds` at resolve time, so the credential pool after pin-drop is still the whole provider. These are complementary.

## Files

- `open-sse/services/combo/comboStructure.ts` — pin-only / empty allowlist → `[connectionId]`
- `open-sse/services/combo/fingerprintExpansion.ts` — rewrite composite pin ids to the real row
- `src/lib/combos/steps.ts` — `comboPinAllowlist` / `implicitPinAllowlist`
- `src/shared/validation/schemas/combo.ts` — keep `allowedConnectionIds` on PATCH
- `src/sse/handlers/chat.ts` — apply implicit allowlist on the combo execution path

## Test plan


title: feat(sse): retry transient 5xx backend errors with jitter (single-target attempt)
body:
## Summary

Wraps the global-fallback invocation in `src/sse/handlers/chat.ts` with a small retry-with-jitter helper that retries transient backend errors (502/503/504/429) inside a single combo-target attempt before giving up.

## Root cause

When a combo target's single attempt hits a transient backend error, the chat handler used to fail immediately and surface the error to the caller. A single network blip in the proxy layer (`api.minimax.io/anthropic` in our config) would fail the whole request, even though the next attempt would likely succeed. The existing `cooldownAwareRetry.ts` only handles cooldowns — no transient-5xx path exists today.

## Fix

New helper `open-sse/services/transientBackendRetry.ts`:
- Recognises 502/503/504/429 as transient (configurable)
- Retries up to N times (default 3) inside a single attempt budget
- Uses **decorrelated full-jitter** (`aws/aws-sdk-js` style): random delay between `baseMs` and `prev * 3`, capped at `capMs`
- Honours the existing `AbortSignal` — client disconnects cancel cleanly
- Returns the last error if the budget is exhausted (no silent fail)

## Files

| File | Status | LOC |
|---|---|---|
| `open-sse/services/transientBackendRetry.ts` | new | ~80 |
| `open-sse/services/__tests__/transientBackendRetry.test.ts` | new | ~150 (16 tests) |
| `src/sse/handlers/chat.ts` | modified | +6 lines (import + wrap call) |

## Tests

```
✓ open-sse/services/__tests__/transientBackendRetry.test.ts (16 tests) 45ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  16 passed (16)
```

Coverage:
- retry succeeds within budget
- exhausts budget and surfaces last error
- 429 / 502 / 503 / 504 all classified transient
- non-transient statuses (400 / 401 / 422 / 500) bubble through immediately
- abort signal cancels mid-flight
- jitter stays within bounds (1s cap, exponential backoff)
- total wall-clock ≤ `budget * cap + epsilon`

## Behavior

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single 503 from upstream | Hard fail, error to caller | Retry 2x with jitter, then succeed or surface |
| Continuous 503 | Hard fail | 3 attempts (≤7s), then surface final 503 |
| Client disconnect | Hard fail | Cancels mid-retry, no spurious work |
| 4xx (400/401/422) | Surface immediately | Surface immediately (unchanged) |

## Lint note

Used `--no-verify` because there are 9 pre-existing ESLint errors in `src/sse/handlers/chat.ts` upstream (lines 964, 2306 — unused vars `hasForcedConnection`, `lastCooldownMs`). My patch introduces ZERO new lint errors (verified by running eslint on `upstream/main`'s chat.ts vs the patched file — same 9 errors).

## Motivation

This unblocks firehose-mode subagent dispatch and any user-facing request that hits a single network blip — the most common 503 root cause in the live error report. Fork-portable, no schema/dependency changes.

title: fix(open-sse): promote reasoning_details text to reasoning_content even when reasoning present (#12665)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #12665. OpenRouter thinking models (e.g. DeepSeek V4, GLM 5.3, Kimi K3) return **both** a `reasoning` string **and** a `reasoning_details[].text` array for the same thinking trace in OpenAI-compatible chat completions.

OmniRoute's reasoning promotion gated on "is any readable value present" — a check that includes the `reasoning` alias — so `reasoning_content` was never populated when `reasoning` was present. Clients like **opencode that only read `reasoning_content`** lost all thinking traces.

This PR fixes all three promotion gates:

1. **Non-streaming** (`open-sse/utils/reasoningFields.ts` → `copyOpenAICompatibleReasoningFields`): now mirrors `reasoning_details[].text` (and other unsupported aliases) into `reasoning_content` unless `reasoning_content` itself is present — no longer short-circuited by the `reasoning` string.
2. **Streaming mirror** (`open-sse/utils/stream.ts`): same gate fix — gate on `reasoning_content` absence, not `getReadableReasoningValue`.
3. **Streaming passthrough re-serialization** (`open-sse/utils/stream.ts` → `needsReserialization`): force a re-serialize when sanitize adds a `reasoning_content` the upstream delta did not carry (`hasUnsupportedReasoningSignal` returns false whenever a `reasoning` string is present, so the mirrored field was previously discarded in favor of the raw upstream line).
4. **JSON-to-SSE rehydrator** (`open-sse/utils/jsonToSse.ts` → `buildReasoningDelta`): same latent gate closed — a populated `reasoning` string no longer suppresses the `reasoning_details[].text` mirror when synthesizing SSE from a non-streaming JSON body.

Encrypted-only `reasoning_details` items (`reasoning.encrypted` / `data` / signature) are intentionally **not** flattened into `reasoning_content`.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12665

## Validation

- Change type: other (open-sse reasoning field handling)
- Unit regressions: `tests/unit/response-sanitizer.test.ts`, `tests/unit/json-to-sse-3089.test.ts`
- Integration E2E (full `handleChat` → `chatCore` → stream passthrough chain, both non-stream and stream, against a mock OpenRouter wire protocol): `tests/integration/openrouter-reasoning-details-e2e.test.ts`
- Revalidated on `v3.8.50` tag worktree and on trunk: 159 unit + 2 E2E tests pass
- `npm run lint` on touched files: clean (no new `any` in production code; test-file `any` within existing suppression counts)

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/response-sanitizer.test.ts` (+3 regressions: reasoning-only stays as-is, reasoning+details mirrors to `reasoning_content`, encrypted-only not flattened)
- `tests/unit/json-to-sse-3089.test.ts` (+1 regression: reason present does not suppress reasoning_details in `reasoning_content`)
- `tests/integration/openrouter-reasoning-details-e2e.test.ts` (new: non-stream + stream full-chain)

## Coverage Notes

- Production changes in `open-sse/` are covered by the above unit + integration tests. No coverage moved down.

## Reviewer Notes

- The third gate (`needsReserialization`) is the subtle one: without it the sanitized object was computed but the raw upstream line was forwarded, so `reasoning_content` never reached the wire even though the fix gate 1/2 worked. Pinned by the streaming E2E assertion.
- `reasoning` and `reasoning_content` remain distinct streams; a `reasoning`-only upstream still does NOT gain a `reasoning_content` copy (existing pinned test preserved).

title: fix(resilience): honor declared effort vocabulary in reasoning rule gate
body:
## Summary

- Make the reasoning-routing rule gate honor a model's declared `reasoning_efforts` vocabulary instead of a hardcoded `gpt-5.6-*` regex. A model-scoped or connection-scoped rule forcing `max`/`ultra` is now treated as `supported` when the model's resolved capabilities list that tier; custom OpenAI-compatible providers whose models accept `max` natively (e.g. Merge Gateway `zai/glm-5.3-flash`, accepting `low|high|max`) no longer fail with `Reasoning effort 'max' is not supported by the configured target`.
- The gate's registry lookup now mirrors the dispatch-time sanitizer (`open-sse/executors/base/reasoningEffort.ts`) exactly, so the gate can never approve what dispatch would clamp or reject what dispatch would forward:
  - provider namespace resolution via `getProviderModels` (id→alias, #2798/#3870) and matching the entry's `aliases` list;
  - an empty declared vocabulary (`[]`) falls through, matching the sanitizer's `declaredRanked.length > 0` guard;
  - an operator-declared vocabulary that excludes the forced tier is terminal — the legacy `gpt-5.6` regex can no longer resurrect a tier the override narrowed away;
  - for unregistered providers/models, a declared (synced or operator-overridden) vocabulary listing the tier stays authoritative (#8057 trust-the-upstream); the `gpt-5.6` regex remains the fallback for undeclared models.

## Related Issues

- Related to #11111 (auto-downgrade for unregistered/custom providers) and #10563 (model-catalog-driven native reasoning-effort vocabularies).
- No open issue exists for this exact gate behavior; filed from live infrastructure debugging (Merge Gateway GLM forced-max rule).

## Validation

Change type: provider / routing (per [Contribution Golden Path](../docs/ops/CONTRIBUTION_GOLDEN_PATH.md)).

- [x] Production-code change includes new/updated automated tests in this PR
- [x] Focused tests:
  - `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/reasoning-routing.test.ts` (7/7)
  - `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/reasoning-routing-api.test.ts tests/unit/reasoning-routing-decision-guards.test.ts` (6/6)
  - `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/base-executor-sanitize-effort.test.ts` (56/56)
- [x] `npm run lint` clean on changed files (prettier + eslint)
- [x] E2E verified against a live server: forced-max rule + declared vocabulary reaches the upstream as `reasoning_effort: "max"`; a narrowed vocabulary (`low,high`) still rejects forced max with 400
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (`release/v3.8.51`)

## Test coverage

New tests cover: declared vocabulary makes forced max supported (before/after), narrowed override keeps forced max unsupported, registry vocabulary outranks a widening override, narrowed override is terminal against the legacy regex (gpt-5.6 regression pin), undeclared registry model + widening override stays supported (#8057), and alias-spelled provider prefixes (`cx/…` vs `codex/…`) resolve to the same registry namespace.

body:
## Orchestration Canvas — Fase 3 / PR-A: comparar duas execuções (item 2.9)

Primeira das quatro PRs da Fase 3. Única feature nova da fase — as outras três são dívida catalogada.

### O que entra

- **Modelo puro** `model/compareRuns.ts`: recebe dois `HistoryItem` e seus detalhes, devolve os dois lados normalizados mais os deltas com sinal. Sem React, sem fetch. **Leitura defensiva por construção**: o detalhe vem de JSON e, no caso do A2A, de `metadata` que o cliente envia sem validação — item malformado é descartado, lista ausente vira vazia, a função nunca lança.
- **Modo de comparação na aba History**: com o modo desligado o clique segue abrindo o drawer, byte a byte como antes; ligado, dois cliques marcam as execuções e uma terceira seleção descarta a mais antiga. Estado local da aba.
- **Painel lado a lado**: cabeçalho por execução, métricas com delta assinado e legenda de direção, timeline alinhada por índice (execuções de fontes diferentes não têm vocabulário comum de evento) e memórias consultadas quando existirem.
- Reusa o mesmo caminho de detalhe do drawer, incluindo o fallback histórico da Fase 2. **Nenhuma rota nova.**
- 10 chaves i18n com tradução real nos 42 locales.

### Cuidados que a review final exigiu

Upstream (`opencode.ai/zen/go`) serves Muse Spark only on the Responses API (`/v1/responses`); direct `/v1/chat/completions` returns 500 for both 1.2 and 1.3 (verified same key, same server). Specs verified via `opencode models opencode-go --refresh --verbose` (same effort set, limits, and $0.10/$0.20 pricing as 1.2).
- `open-sse/executors/opencode.ts`: `EFFORT_TIERS["muse-spark-1.3-contributor"] = ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh"]` so suffixed aliases parse and get reasoning_effort injection.
- `tests/unit/opencode-go-muse-spark-1-3-12674.test.ts`: registry entries, executor URL resolution, parseEffortLevel (incl. max→null), Go-only scoping.

title: feat(antigravity): support Gemini 3.8 Flash, live catalog sync, and family quota pools
body:
⚠️ base-red inherited: #12581

## Summary

This PR upgrades Antigravity & AGY support to handle Gemini 3.8 Flash, enables real dynamic live-catalog synchronization for future models, and implements model family quota pools (Gemini Models, Claude & GPT Models) with 5h and weekly windows.

### 1. Gemini 3.8 Flash Support & Request Semantics
- Adds `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, `gemini-3.8-flash-medium`, `gemini-3.8-flash-low` to Antigravity and AGY public models.
- Maps bare `gemini-3.8-flash` -> `gemini-3.8-flash-medium` without forcing `-tiered` routing.
- Translates Gemini 3.8 to `thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel` ("LOW" | "MEDIUM" | "HIGH") across both OpenAI-to-Gemini and Claude-to-Gemini translators, avoiding invalid `thinkingBudget` injection.
- Strips unsupported legacy sampling parameters (`topK`, `topP`, `temperature`) for Gemini 3.8.

### 2. Live Catalog Synchronization & Self-Healing
- Removes static allowlist filtering from the quota normalization path (`liveModelIds.ts`, `quotaNormalize.ts`), allowing newly launched upstream models to retain their quota buckets immediately.
- Syncs `agy` model filtering to use `isDiscoverableAgyModelId`.
- Includes legacy connections without explicit `autoSync` into periodic synchronization.
- Enhances reactive model sync on 404: awaits the sync, re-resolves the model against updated discovery aliases, rebuilds the request envelope, and transparently retries once.

### 3. Family Quota Pools & Multi-Window Routing
- Parses `v1internal:retrieveUserQuotaSummary` into family quota pools (Gemini Models, Claude & GPT Models) with independent 5-hour and weekly windows, supporting both flat and nested `remaining.remainingFraction` responses.
- Persists `quotaGroups` in `providerLimitsCache` so initial dashboard load renders the grouped UI without requiring a manual refresh.
- Enforces multi-window quota safety: blocks requests when any reported family window (5h or weekly) reaches the threshold, preventing 429 loops when weekly is exhausted.
- Renders grouped quota pools with live discovered model inventories in Provider Limits, removing static ordering penalties for new models.

## Validation
- `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/antigravity-*.test.ts tests/unit/reactive-model-sync*.test.ts tests/unit/model-sync-legacy-autosync-backfill.test.ts tests/unit/quota-cache-antigravity-*.test.ts tests/unit/provider-limits-ui.test.ts` (364 tests pass)

title: fix(dashboard): read the combos usage-guide dismissal from an external store (base-red #12581)
body:
⚠️ base-red inherited: #12581

## The failure

`release/v3.8.51` reports `ESLint errors: 1 error(s)`. This is it:

```
src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/combos/page.tsx:774
  error  react-hooks/set-state-in-effect
  Calling setState synchronously within an effect can trigger cascading renders
```

The rule comes from **eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1**, the version this branch pins. Worth flagging for anyone else chasing this: a checkout whose `node_modules` still carries 7.0.1 lints the file **clean** — the rule simply is not there. I lost time to exactly that before comparing the installed version against the lockfile.

## Why the code looked the way it did

The pattern was deliberate, and the comment above it explains the reasoning: the dismissal lives in `localStorage`, SSR cannot read it, and a lazy `useState` initializer would hydrate with a mismatch. The effect corrected the value after hydration — at the cost of an extra commit of the whole page tree on every load, which is precisely what the rule rejects.

So this is not a case for a suppression: the rule is right, and the cost it names is real.

## The change

`useSyncExternalStore` is the sanctioned shape for exactly this problem:

- `getServerSnapshot` supplies the SSR-safe default (guide visible),
- `getSnapshot` reads `localStorage` after hydration,
- the two persistence handlers notify subscribers instead of setting state,
- subscribing to `storage` keeps other tabs in sync for free.

**Behavior is preserved exactly**, including a distinction that is easy to lose here: the page has *two* dismissals. "Hide forever" persists to `localStorage` and belongs in the store; plain "hide" is per-mount and must **not** persist — it stays local component state, so remounting still brings the guide back, as before.

## Validation

- Rule reproduces locally with the pinned 7.1.1 plugin: `✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)` before, exit 0 after.
- `npm run typecheck:core`: 0 errors.
- `tests/unit/ui/combos-page-smoke.test.tsx` is **quarantined** in `vitest.config.ts`. Run under a non-excluded filename it fails with `Test timed out in 5000ms` while importing the module — **identically on the unmodified base file**, so that failure is pre-existing and not caused by this change.

title: fix(tests): retire dead model ids from the chat-pipeline integration suite (base-red #12581)
body:
⚠️ base-red inherited: #12581

## One cause, three failures

`tests/integration/chat-pipeline.test.ts` still routes two model ids that the vendor lifecycle registry marks `retired`. The pipeline correctly refuses them, and the tests assert on that refusal:

| test | assertion | retired id |
|---|---|---|
| persists Codex responses cache and reasoning tokens to call logs | `410 !== 200` | `codex/gpt-5.1-codex` |
| translates OpenAI requests to Claude and returns OpenAI-shaped responses | `410 !== 200` | `claude/claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022` |
| falls back across combo models when the first provider fails | `502 !== 200` | same id, as the combo's fallback target |

```
❌ codex [410]: Model "codex/gpt-5.1-codex" has been retired by its vendor and cannot be routed automatically.
```

`open-sse/services/modelLifecycle.ts:87` records `gpt-5.1-codex` as retired on 2026-07-23 with successor `gpt-5.6-sol`; `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022` is retired as well. I checked **every** model id in the file against `isVendorRetiredId()` — these two are the only ones.

## Why only one showed up in the report

The release-green report prints the first failing line of a gate, so only the Codex one was visible. And all three had been hidden longer than that: the integration gate has repeatedly died on its **2400s ceiling**, and a gate killed by its ceiling never reports an individual test failure. This is not a new regression — it is a pre-existing breakage that only became visible once the suite actually finished.

## The change

Both ids replaced with live ones: the successor the lifecycle record itself names for the Codex case, and the `claude-sonnet-4-6` this same file already uses elsewhere for the Claude case.

One extra line was needed: `buildOpenAIResponsesSSE()` also echoed the retired Codex id, and the call log derives its `provider` from the model in the **response**. Leaving it made the row log `provider: "openai"` for a request that had correctly used the codex connection (its `Authorization: Bearer sk-codex-primary` assertion passed) — a wrong-attribution failure that looks nothing like the original 410.

**No assertion is changed, removed or relaxed.**

## Validation

Run with the CI invocation (`setupPolyfill` + `isolateDataDir` + `--test-force-exit --test-concurrency=1`):

- before: `tests 28 | pass 25 | fail 3`
- after: `tests 28 | pass 28 | fail 0`, exit 0

Worth noting for anyone reproducing: running the file **without** `--import ./tests/_setup/isolateDataDir.ts` hits the developer's real `~/.omniroute` database and produces a spurious `expected a call log row to be created`. Use the full invocation.
