title: fix(gemini): strip prefixItems from Gemini tool schemas
body:
## Summary

- `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` (`open-sse/translator/helpers/geminiHelper.ts:9-105` on the base) is the only strip-list `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` applies to tool parameter schemas (`removeUnsupportedKeywords`, `geminiHelper.ts:643`), and it did not contain the JSON-Schema-2020-12 tuple keyword `prefixItems`. Claude Code's built-in tools describe `[start_line, end_line]` ranges as a tuple nested under `items`, so every tool-bearing Claude Code request routed to a Gemini model was rejected before generation with `400 Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "prefixItems" at 'tools[0].function_declarations[1].parameters.properties[5].value.properties[0].value.items': Cannot find field` (#12509). All three tool shapes that `buildGeminiTools` accepts go through the same cleaner (`geminiToolsSanitizer.ts:207`, `:220` for Claude `input_schema`, `:238` for OpenAI `function.parameters`), so the Claude Messages compatibility path the reporter uses and the OpenAI path were both affected.
- Before: `prefixItems` survived at every nesting level (top-level array property, sibling of `items`, and the reporter's tuple under `items`) and reached Gemini verbatim. After: `prefixItems` is added to `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` next to `uniqueItems` (#9617), so it is removed recursively at every level, the same way `multipleOf`, `strict` and `encrypted` already are. When the tuple carried `items: false` (the 2020-12 idiom for "no extra elements"), Phase 8 `ensureArrayItems` (`geminiHelper.ts:733` on the base) already injects `{ type: "string" }`, so the parameter stays a valid Gemini array with an `items` schema; when a regular `items` schema sits next to `prefixItems`, that `items` schema is kept untouched.
- Deliberately out of scope: promoting `prefixItems[0]` into `items` (the tuple's element types can differ, and Gemini has no way to express positional typing, so the safe default `items` schema is the honest translation); touching `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_CONSTRAINTS` beyond what it already derives from the Set; any change to the Antigravity envelope or to response schemas.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12509
- Related to #9617 (same class of fix, `uniqueItems`)
- Related to #12310 (touches the same file; see Reviewer Notes)

## Validation

Choose the change type and focused loop from the
[Contribution Golden Path](../docs/ops/CONTRIBUTION_GOLDEN_PATH.md). The full unit suite,
Vitest, the 60% coverage gate, and the production build all run in CI on this PR (#8329):

title: fix(audio): resolve combo names on /v1/audio/translations
body:
## Summary

- `POST /v1/audio/translations` rejected combo names that `GET /v1/models` advertises. On the base, `src/app/api/v1/audio/translations/route.ts:68-77` hands the raw `model` string to `parseTranslationModel()` and returns `400 Invalid translation model: <combo>. Use format: provider/model` when it is not a `provider/model` id; nothing calls `getComboByName()` first. Every sibling already resolves combos: chat, embeddings, `/v1/audio/transcriptions` (#9134, fixed by #9382 at `src/app/api/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:183-212`), `/v1/audio/speech` and `/v1/videos/generations` (#10469, fixed by #10471). Translations was the one route those fixes did not cover, so the same combo name with the same file worked on `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and failed on `/v1/audio/translations`.
- Before: `model=traducao` (a `priority` combo over `localstt/whisper-1`) → `400 Invalid translation model: traducao. Use format: provider/model`, no upstream call. After: one upstream call to `http://localhost:9000/v1/audio/translations` whose multipart `model` is `whisper-1`; the response is the upstream body. Literal `provider/model` ids skip the lookup and unknown bare names keep the existing 400 and format hint.
- The change mirrors the transcriptions route exactly. The single-target body of `POST` moves unchanged into `translateWithModel(formData, modelStr, startTime)`; after `enforceApiKeyPolicy`, a bare name (no `/`) is looked up with `getComboByName()` and, when it is a combo, fanned out through `handleComboChat()` with one multipart copy per target (`withModel()` copies every field and replaces only `model`; the uploaded Blob is reused). Unknown bare names and literal ids fall through to `translateWithModel()` as before. No handler, registry, provider, schema or response-shape change.
- Deliberately out of scope: the alias-candidate credential fallback that transcriptions has (`audioModelAliasCandidates` / `findAlternateAudioProvider`) is not added here, since translations never had it and it is a separate behavior; `withModel()` and the combo block are duplicated from the transcriptions route rather than lifted into `_shared/`, to keep this diff mirror-shaped and reviewable against #9382 (a follow-up could factor both routes onto one helper).

## Related Issues

- Closes: no open issue for this route (open issues and PRs searched for `audio translations combo`; none found).

body:
## Summary

- `DEFAULT_DEGRADATION_MAP` (`open-sse/services/backgroundTaskDetector.ts:52-65`) is the third hand-maintained routing table that names model ids, and it sat outside the retired-model gate from #11503 / #11507: `scripts/check/check-model-lifecycle.mjs` only diffed `FITNESS_TABLE` and `BUILT_IN_ALIASES` against `config/quality/model-lifecycle.json`. Nothing stopped a background-task redirect row from naming a model the vendor has retired.
- Three rows named a retired source: `claude-sonnet-4-20250514 → gemini-3-flash` (retired 2026-06-15), `gemini-3-pro-preview → gemini-3-flash-preview` (retired, no date in the snapshot) and `gpt-5.1-codex → gpt-5.1-codex-mini` (both ends retired). They were dead code: `checkLifecycle` (`open-sse/handlers/chatCore.ts:791-792`) answers 410 `model_shutdown` (`open-sse/handlers/chatCore/modelLifecyclePolicy.ts:31-37`) before `resolveBackgroundTaskRedirect` runs (`chatCore.ts:831`), so no request carrying one of those ids ever reached the redirect. Dropping them changes nothing user-visible. No row had a retired target under a live source, so no forwarding decision was needed.

The map now carries a comment pointing at the gate (`backgroundTaskDetector.ts:48-51`).
- Deliberately out of scope: `src/lib/config/runtimeSettings.ts:324-329` still spreads `getDefaultDegradationMap()` under the stored map, so a default row an operator removed in the dashboard comes back on restart (#12424). This PR keeps the *defaults* clean; it does not change how stored maps are merged, and it does not purge the three rows from a stored map that was saved with them. `gemini-3.1-pro-high` (`backgroundTaskDetector.ts:60`, a non-catalog spelling that is not retired) is left as is. The current allowlist question in #12436 is about check (c) and is untouched.

title: feat(resilience): surface TLS-fingerprint remediation when Cloudflare 1010 hits
body:
Fixes #12529

## Summary

A Cloudflare `403` / `error_code 1010` rejection means the CDN banned the CLIENT's TLS/UA signature — not the account. #9929 already classifies this as `FINGERPRINT_REJECTION` so it no longer poisons account state, and the repo already ships the actual fix: a Chrome-124 TLS impersonation transport (`open-sse/utils/tlsClient.ts` via the optional `wreq-js` dependency). But the transport is off unless `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true`, the dependency is optional, and **nothing anywhere connects a 1010 to that fix** — operators see benign-classified 403s and the one-line remediation stays hidden.

This PR emits a **throttled (once-per-process) remediation hint** when a response is classified `FINGERPRINT_REJECTION` while `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT` is not enabled:

```
[errorClassifier] Cloudflare fingerprint rejection (1010 / browser-signature ban) detected.
Remediation: install the optional 'wreq-js' dependency and set ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true
(plus TLS_FINGERPRINT_PROVIDERS=<providers> to cover proxied egress) so egress presents a browser TLS fingerprint.
```

## Change

- `open-sse/services/errorClassifier.ts`: `maybeEmitFingerprintRemediationHint()` called in the fingerprint-rejection branch; module-level once-flag with `resetFingerprintRemediationHintForTest()` seam; hint suppressed entirely when the transport is enabled.
- `tests/unit/error-classifier.test.ts`: regression test pinning classify-unchanged, throttle-to-once, message contents (`wreq-js`, `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true`), and suppression when enabled.
- `tests/unit/12529-fingerprint-remediation-auth-path.test.ts`: regression on the **auth.ts consumer path** (maintainer request on #12529) — drives `markAccountUnavailable` end-to-end with a real Cloudflare-1010 403 and asserts the account stays active/non-terminal **and** the hint fires from that path.
- `changelog.d/fixes/12529-tls-fingerprint-remediation-hint.md`.

No classification, combo-routing, or account-state changes (#9929 behavior untouched). No new dependencies (wreq-js is already an optionalDependency).

## Testing

- `node --test` with the repo loader stack (`tsx/esm` + polyfills):
  - `tests/unit/error-classifier.test.ts` — **35/35 pass** (34 baseline + 1 new).
  - `tests/unit/12529-fingerprint-remediation-auth-path.test.ts` — **3/3 pass**: 1010 through `markAccountUnavailable` keeps the connection active/non-terminal (`banned`/`expired`/`credits_exhausted` all asserted against) **and** emits exactly one hint containing `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true` and `wreq-js`; repeated 1010s stay throttled to one emission; suppressed entirely when `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true`.
- Branch merged current `release/v3.8.51` (merge state was DIRTY; now MERGEABLE — includes upstream's #10725 Kiro IDC block in the same 403 region).

## Deployment evidence

On the affected production instance: enabling `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true` (wreq-js present since install) switched direct egress to the Chrome-124 fingerprint — verified via `tls.peet.ws/api/all`:

- wreq-js `chrome_124` session: `ja3_hash 24a38702f3a11cf1d1c52478881cb992` (browser UA, h2)
- Node default fetch: `ja3_hash d67b094811e5145139d7cea5f014309f`

1010 rejections stopped after enablement. For the Python-stack variant of this phenomenon (urllib flagged, curl passes), `curl_cffi`'s browser impersonation is the equivalent client-side fix — noted for completeness in #12529.

title: fix(docker): fix Bun variant build, SQLite runtime and process.execPath startup on main
body:
### Summary

Fixes multiple failure modes preventing the Docker Bun variant (`Dockerfile.bun`) from building and starting on `main`:

1. **`run-standalone.mjs` runtime resolution**: Replaced hardcoded `spawnWithForwardedSignals("node", [entry], ...)` with `process.execPath`. In `oven/bun:*-slim` containers, `node` is absent from PATH, causing an immediate startup crash (`spawn node ENOENT`).
2. **Runner base image version**: Bumped `runner-base` from `oven/bun:1.3.14-slim` to `oven/bun:1.4.0-slim` to match the `base` stage and latest Bun runtime.
3. **`better-sqlite3` native addon elimination for Bun**: Under Bun, OmniRoute uses the native `bun:sqlite` database driver. Stripped vendored `better-sqlite3` binaries from the runner image to prevent dlopen/NAPI crashes prior to driver fallback.
4. **Builder layer caching & smoke checks**: Added dependency layer caching prior to `bun install` and replaced fragile native rebuild steps with `wreq-js` binding verification and native `bun:sqlite` smoke checks.
5. **Security & permissions**: Enforced non-root `USER bun` execution with `chown -R bun:bun /app /app/data`.

### Tests & Validation

- `tests/unit/build/bun-runtime-native-addon.test.mjs`: Verifies `Dockerfile.bun` removes `better-sqlite3` native addons and excludes them from the runner.
- `tests/unit/build/run-standalone-execpath.test.mjs`: Verifies `run-standalone.mjs` spawns with `process.execPath` instead of hardcoded `"node"`.
- `tests/unit/docker-build-memory-budget.test.ts`: 8/8 tests pass (verifies memory budget across both `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.bun`).
- `tests/unit/bun-support.test.ts`: 4/4 tests pass.
- `npm run typecheck:core` & `npm run lint` & `npm run check:docs-all`: Clean (0 errors).

title: fix(rerank): clamp Voyage top_k and honor NVIDIA return_documents
body:
## Summary

- Two rerank adapter defects in `open-sse/handlers/rerank.ts`, both on the current `release/v3.8.51` base:
  - **Voyage `top_k` exceeds the documents sent.** `handleRerank` normalizes `top_n: top_n || documents.length` from the caller's *unfiltered* array (`rerank.ts:237`) before the request adapter runs; the Voyage adapter then drops exact empty strings (`rerank.ts:80-82`) but still emits `top_k: body.top_n || docTexts.length` (`rerank.ts:87`), i.e. the unfiltered count. `POST /v1/rerank` with `documents: ["a", "", "b"]` and no `top_n` sends 2 documents with `top_k: 3`; Voyage rejects `top_k > documents.length` with HTTP 400 and the caller sees a gateway failure for a request that is valid under the Cohere-style contract this endpoint exposes. The same happens for an explicit `top_n` larger than the surviving count.
  - **NVIDIA ignores `return_documents: false`.** The NVIDIA response adapter always emits `document: { text }` (`rerank.ts:109`), while its deepinfra (`rerank.ts:121,128`) and voyage (`rerank.ts:147,163`) siblings gate the field on `options.return_documents !== false`, and the handler already passes `return_documents` into the adapter for every provider. Callers that opt out of document echo still get the full text back on NVIDIA.
- After: the Voyage request adapter clamps `top_k` to `Math.min(body.top_n || docTexts.length, docTexts.length)`, so a legitimate `top_n` below the count is untouched and only the impossible case is corrected; the NVIDIA response adapter gates `document` exactly like deepinfra and voyage. Default behavior (`return_documents` omitted or `true`) is unchanged.
- Out of scope: the `top_n || documents.length` default in the handler (it is correct for every other provider, which does not drop documents), Voyage's handling of whitespace-only documents (accepted and ranked upstream, see #7809), and any change to `index` remapping or score ordering.

## Related Issues

- Closes: none. No open issue tracks either defect (open issues searched for `rerank`, `voyage top_k`, `return_documents`).
- Related to #7809, #7811 (Voyage adapter: empty-string filtering and `top_k` mapping), #5332 (NVIDIA/deepinfra adapters and the `return_documents` gate on deepinfra)

## Validation

Choose the change type and focused loop from the
[Contribution Golden Path](../docs/ops/CONTRIBUTION_GOLDEN_PATH.md). The full unit suite,
Vitest, the 60% coverage gate, and the production build all run in CI on this PR (#8329):

- [x] Change type: provider (rerank request/response adapters in `open-sse/handlers/rerank.ts`)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: `tests/unit/rerank-*.test.ts` 46/46 (12 files, 3 suites); `npm run check:provider-consistency` OK; `npm run check:provider-assets` OK; `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK (new-code violations 0/0); `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK; `npm run typecheck:core` exit 0; `eslint` on the three touched files exit 0
- [ ] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51` (rebased onto `86e83d413`, no conflicts); focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

Red/green: with the base `rerank.ts` swapped in, the two touched test files report 25 pass / 3 fail — exactly the three new cases that encode the defects (`nvidia … return_documents=false`, `voyage … clamps top_k to the surviving document count`, `voyage … clamps an explicit oversized top_n`). With the change, 28/28.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/rerank-voyage-7809.test.ts` (+3 cases): `top_k` clamped to the surviving count when `top_n` mirrors the handler's unfiltered default (`["a", "", "b"]`, `top_n: 3` → `documents: ["a", "b"]`, `top_k: 2`); an explicit oversized `top_n: 10` with two empty strings is clamped to 2; a legitimate `top_n: 2` over three non-empty documents stays 2.
- `tests/unit/rerank-providers-5332.test.ts` (+3 cases): NVIDIA omits `document` when `return_documents: false` while keeping `index` and `relevance_score`; includes `document.text` when `return_documents: true`; includes it when `return_documents` is omitted (default preserved).
- `changelog.d/fixes/PENDING-rerank-topk-and-return-documents.md`: changelog fragment; the `PENDING` prefix will be replaced with this PR's number.

## Coverage Notes

- `open-sse/handlers/rerank.ts`: the Voyage `top_k` expression is exercised by the three new `transformRequestForProvider` cases (clamped, clamped from explicit oversized, not clamped); the NVIDIA `returnDocuments` branch is exercised in both directions plus the omitted-option default by the three new `transformResponseFromProvider` cases. Existing cases in both files (empty-string filtering, index remapping, sorting, `top_n` honoring, deepinfra gate) are unchanged and green.
- No touched file lost coverage; the change adds one branch per adapter and both branches of each are covered.

## Reviewer Notes

- Both changes are confined to the two provider-specific adapters; no shared handler path, endpoint, registry, or other provider changes.
- The clamp uses `Math.min` on the already-computed value rather than moving the `top_n` default into the adapter, so the handler's normalization (and the `top_n` logged in `saveCallLog`) is untouched; only the value sent to Voyage changes.
- The NVIDIA gate follows the sibling adapters verbatim (`options.return_documents !== false`), so a missing option keeps today's behavior of returning the text.
- No live call against Voyage or NVIDIA was made for this PR; the 400 is documented Voyage behavior for `top_k > len(documents)` and the tests assert the request payload shape rather than the provider response.

title: feat(gamification): pay the documented streak and badge XP rewards
body:
## Summary

- `XP_REWARDS` (`src/lib/gamification/xp.ts:155-158`) documents `streak_bonus` ("per consecutive streak day, multiplied by streak length") and `badge_unlock`, but the award pipeline never paid either: `events.ts` kept a private reward table without them (`getXpForAction`), `updateStreak()` did not report whether the streak had just extended, and `checkAndUnlockBadge()` unlocked badges with no XP.
- Every request that extends a daily streak now pays `streak_bonus × streak length` once per UTC day; every badge unlocked through the pipeline pays `badge_unlock` once per badge. Bonus XP goes through the same `addXp` + level sync + global/weekly/monthly leaderboard path as action XP, so level-ups and rankings include it.
- Idempotency: `advanceStreak()` reports `extended` only on the call that moves the record to today, and a same-day `xp_audit_log` check is evaluated and inserted synchronously; `unlockBadge()` now returns whether it inserted the `(api_key_id, badge_id)` row, and XP is paid only then. Restarts and duplicate events cannot double-pay.
- The Radar supporter recognition unlock stays XP-free, as its comment requires. No other scoring changes; `getXpForAction`, badge thresholds and `evaluateBadges()` are untouched. Amounts follow `XP_REWARDS` (2 × streak, 10 per badge). The docs table (`docs/frameworks/GAMIFICATION.md:239-252`) names different rewards and amounts; that is tracked separately in #12501, and which table is authoritative is the maintainer's call. If the docs values win, the two constants in `XP_REWARDS` are the only place that changes: the award path introduced here reads them and nothing else. Deliberately out of scope: wiring `evaluateBadges()` (no callers; it would change which badges unlock and needs `badge_definitions` seeded at startup), retroactive bonus for streaks already in progress, paying on day 1 of a streak. Step 1 of `emitGamificationEvent` is unchanged, so #12390's rate-limit gate applies cleanly; extending it to bonus XP is a one-line follow-up in `awardBonusXp` once it lands.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12426
- Related to #12501 (docs table, split out by the maintainer)
- Related to #2403

## Validation

- [x] Change type: Backend (gamification award pipeline) + DB helper
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: `tests/unit/gamification/*.test.ts` 98/98 (37 suites, 14 files), `npm run check:db-rules` OK, `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK, `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK, `npm run typecheck:core` 0
- [x] `npm run lint` — repository-wide eslint exit 0 (run with `--pass-on-unpruned-suppressions`; the literal command reports only pre-existing unused global suppressions on this base)
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51`; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

Mutation: removing the two award calls fails 5 of the 9 new tests (the 4 that pass are plumbing and negatives).

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/gamification/streak-badge-xp.test.ts` (new, 9 cases): `advanceStreak` extension reporting; `streak_bonus × n` paid with `{streak}` metadata and credited to `user_levels` + global/weekly/monthly; once per UTC day across repeated requests; no bonus on day 1 or after a broken streak; `unlockBadge` insert reporting; `badge_unlock` paid once per badge with `{badgeId}` metadata; streak badge + bonus from the same request; level recomputed after bonus XP (280 + 1 stays level 1, + badge XP crosses 282); `radar_supporter` path stays XP-free. Red on the base (5 fail / 4 pass), green with the change (9/9). Existing `streaks.test.ts`, `events.test.ts`, `badge-unlock-once-3472.test.ts` unchanged and green.

## Coverage Notes

- `src/lib/gamification/events.ts`: new `syncLevel`, `awardBonusXp`, `awardStreakBonus` and the `checkAndUnlockBadge` payment branch are exercised end-to-end through `emitGamificationEvent` in the new test file.
- `src/lib/gamification/streaks.ts`: `advanceStreak` covered directly and via the pipeline; `updateStreak` remains covered by `streaks.test.ts`.
- `src/lib/db/gamification.ts`: `unlockBadge` return value and `hasXpActionToday` covered by the insert-reporting and once-per-day cases.
- No touched file lost coverage.

title: fix(api): thread X-OmniRoute-Fallback-Attempts through chat completions (#12339)
body:
## Problem

As reported in #12339 by @diegosouzapw:

On `/v1/chat/completions` responses (both streaming `stream: true` and non-streaming `stream: false`), the `X-OmniRoute-Fallback-Attempts` HTTP header is absent (or defaults to `0`), even when a combo failover to a non-primary target occurred before the stream/response opened.

While `X-OmniRoute-Provider` and `X-OmniRoute-Model` update correctly to the winning provider, the fallback attempts counter was completely missing from chat responses.

## Root Cause

1. **Missing parameter in response-header builders:** Both `assembleStreamingResponseHeaders` and `buildNonStreamingResponseHeaders` built metadata headers without accepting or passing `fallbackAttempts` into `buildStreamingResponseHeaders` / `attachOmniRouteMetaHeaders`.

2. **Missing forwarding in `chatCore.ts`:** `handleChatCore` did not accept `fallbackAttempts` or pass it to either header builder.

3. **Dropped in the dispatch chain:** While `open-sse/services/combo.ts` properly calculates `fallbackCount`, it was not passed through `handleSingleModel` (`chat.ts`), `executeChatWithBreaker` (`chatHelpers.ts`), or `dispatchChatWithAffinityEviction`.

## Fix

### 1. Response Header Builders

- **`open-sse/handlers/chatCore/nonStreamingResponseHeaders.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts?: number` to the `args` type.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts: args.fallbackAttempts` to `deps.attachOmniRouteMetaHeaders`.

- **`open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingResponseHeaders.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts?: number` to the `args` type.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts: args.fallbackAttempts` to `buildStreamingResponseHeaders`.

### 2. Core Handler & Dispatch Chain

- **`open-sse/handlers/chatCore.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts = 0` to `handleChatCore` parameters.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts` to `buildNonStreamingResponseHeaders` and `assembleStreamingResponseHeaders`.

- **`src/sse/handlers/chatHelpers.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts = 0` to `executeChatWithBreaker` options.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts` into `handleChatCore`.

- **`src/sse/handlers/chat.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts?: number` to the `target` type in `handleSingleModel`.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts: target?.fallbackAttempts ?? 0` into `handleSingleModelChat`.
  - Added `fallbackAttempts?: number` to the `runtimeOptions` type in `handleSingleModelChat`.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts: runtimeOptions?.fallbackAttempts ?? 0` into `dispatchChatWithAffinityEviction`.

### 3. Combo Layer

- **`open-sse/services/combo.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts: fallbackCount` when dispatching targets in `handleComboChatInner` (`handleSingleModelWithTimeout`).

title: fix(command-code): floor tiny muse-spark output budgets so hidden reasoning cannot consume the whole budget
body:
## Summary

- muse-spark (Meta) models routed through **command-code** burn their entire output budget on invisible server-side reasoning before emitting any visible content. With a small
caller-set `max_tokens` (e.g. 64) the upstream answers HTTP 200 with **null content** (`out=64, reasoning=61`) — the client receives an empty assistant turn and OmniRoute flags the
fake success as "Provider returned empty content". This is the reproduction in **#12130**.
- Fix: reuse the already prefix-aware `MUSE_SPARK_PATTERN` (`/(?:^|\/|\b)muse-spark/i`) to detect muse-spark ids — **including provider-prefixed forms**
(`meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor`, `cmd/meta/muse-…`) that a bare `startsWith("muse-spark")` would miss — and floor a tiny caller budget to `MUSE_SPARK_MIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 512` so
the hidden reasoning phase can never consume the whole budget.
- Applied in **both** command-code body builders: `buildOpenAiBody` (the `/provider/v1/chat/completions` path that the reproduction goes through) and `buildCommandCodeCliBody` (the
`/alpha/generate` 403/404 fallback), mirroring the existing `applyMuseSparkMinOutputTokens` behavior already shipped for the opencode-go executor.

## Related Issues

- Related to #12130 (OpenAI API returns null content when model output consists of reasoning tokens, e.g. `command-code/meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor`) — the exact `out=64,
reasoning=61, content:null` reproduction this fix targets.
- Related to #11214 (muse-spark output budget is floored so it stops returning empty-content responses) — same empty-content-on-small-budget class; previously applied only to
opencode-go, now extended to command-code.
- Related to #10986 (original reasoning-only `content:null` report) — this fix paves the `/provider/v1` path so the budget-floor mitigation prevents the empty-content condition
rather than relying on a downstream fallback.

## Validation

- [x] Change type: provider / routing
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path

  `node --test tests/unit/command-code-executor.test.ts` → 20/20 pass
  `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.typecheck-core.json` → clean
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (`release/v3.8.51`); focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/command-code-executor.test.ts` — 2 new cases:
  - `meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor` + `max_tokens: 64` → raised to `512` (the #12130 bug path)
  - large budget (`4096`) left untouched (no over-flooring)

> The existing `tests/unit/opencode-muse-spark-min-output.test.ts` (11/11 pass) confirms the opencode-go executor is **untouched** — only command-code was modified.

## Coverage Notes

- `open-sse/executors/commandCode.ts` is covered by the two new tests above, exercising `applyMuseSparkMinOutputTokens` on both the floor and no-op paths (bare + prefixed id
detection).
- Full `npm run test:coverage` (global 60% gate) was attempted; the c8 `--merge-async` run stalled into an 8GB `coverage/tmp` on this Windows workstation, so the per-change gates
above (scoped tests + typecheck) were used as the focused loop. The global 60% gate runs in CI on the PR (#8329).

## Reviewer Notes

- Detection now uses the prefix-aware `MUSE_SPARK_PATTERN`. For command-code this is a **superset** of any prior bare-prefix check — no model is exempted, only newly covered (e.g.
the `meta/…` id in this reproduction).
- This PR is the **budget-floor prevention** approach: it stops the empty-content condition for small caller budgets. It does **not** add a reasoning→content fallback inside the
`/provider/v1` raw passthrough for the case where a model emits reasoning-only with a *large* budget — that remains the domain of #10986's fallback (already present on the
`/alpha/generate` path). Maintainer's note in #12130 confirms `/provider/v1` currently returns the upstream `Response` unmodified; if we also want a downstream reasoning→content
fallback there, that is a deliberate follow-up.
- No new dependency, feature flag, DB migration, or manual validation required.

title: fix(devin): treat Devin CLI model ids as literal — never strip or synthesize effort suffixes
body:
## Problem

The Devin CLI providers (`devin-cli`, `devin-cli-agentic`, `devin-desktop`; aliases `dv`/`dva`) serve a catalog whose model ids **embed the reasoning tier**: `claude-opus-5-low`, `claude-opus-5-medium`, … and `gpt-5-6-sol-max`/`-low` are distinct upstream models (see `open-sse/config/providers/registry/devin/catalog.ts`).

Two cross-cutting mechanisms assume a trailing `-{effort}` suffix is a client-side variant, and both corrupt Devin ids:

**1. Dispatch-time strip (`applyClaudeEffortVariant`)** strips the suffix from any id whose base is a known Claude model — correct for the `claude`/`cc` lanes, wrong for Devin. Live evidence from a self-hosted v3.8.51 deployment:

```
POST /v1/chat/completions  model: dva/claude-opus-5-low
→ 400 { "Model is not present in the current Devin catalog: claude-opus-5" }
```

The executor (`assertKnownDevinModel`) rejects the stripped base because upstream has one id **per tier**. Only accidental double-suffixed ids survived (`dva/claude-opus-5-max-low` → strip `-low` → real `claude-opus-5-max`), which made failures look random: `claude-opus-5-low`/`-medium`/`-high`/`-xhigh`/`-max` and the whole `claude-sonnet-5-*` family 400, while `claude-5-fable-*` (a name the static registry doesn't know) worked.

**2. Catalog variant synthesis** advertised phantom ids on top of tier-embedded ids (`dva/gpt-5-6-sol-max-low`, `dva/kimi-k3-*`) that 400 when called.

## Fix

Three gates treat Devin ids as literal, keyed off a single helper (`isDevinLiteralModelIdProvider` — ids + aliases + `provider/model`-qualified prefixes):

- `applyClaudeEffortVariant`: early return for Devin providers — no strip, no `reasoning_effort` mutation.
- `shouldExposeClaudeEffortVariants` (`appendClaudeEffortVariants`): no `-<level>` variants for devin-prefixed ids.
- `isSkippedEffortProvider` (`appendSyncedEffortVariants`): Devin providers join codex/glm/kimi as providers that own their own suffix mechanism — the tier IS the id.

## What does NOT change

- `claude`/`cc` lane stripping (`cc/claude-opus-5-high` → `claude-opus-5` + `reasoning_effort=high`) — untouched, covered by existing + new control tests.
- Non-Devin variant synthesis (OpenCode-style catalog-only clients keep getting `<model>-<level>` ids for Anthropic-served models).

## Tests

- `tests/unit/devin-literal-effort-ids.test.ts` (new): helper matching, both catalog appenders skip Devin entries, `isSkippedEffortProvider` coverage.
- `tests/unit/chatcore-claude-effort-variant.test.ts`: four new cases — devin-cli-agentic keeps `claude-opus-5-low` literal, alias `dva` covered, devin-cli/devin-desktop/`dv` covered, claude-lane control still strips.

## Live validation

Self-hosted v3.8.51 native deployment (before → after): `dva/claude-opus-5-low` 400 → 200, `dva/claude-5-fable-low` unaffected (200 → 200), `dva/swe-1-7` unaffected, phantom variant ids disappear from `/v1/models`, `cc/claude-opus-5-high` routing unchanged.

Note for reviewers: ids like `dva/claude-opus-5-max-low` that previously "worked" by accident will now (correctly) 400 — callers should use the real tier ids (`dva/claude-opus-5-max`, `dva/claude-opus-5-low`, …), which this PR makes selectable in catalog-only clients for the first time.

title: fix(cli): preflight the port before serving so a second instance cannot de-register the first
body:
## Problem

Starting `omniroute serve` against a port another OmniRoute already owns printed three identical raw Node stack traces and no explanation:

```
⚠ Server exited (code=1). Restarting in 1s... (1/2)
⨯ Failed to start server
Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 0.0.0.0:20128
```

The conflict was handed to the child process, so it only surfaced after the child had been spawned and retried twice on the supervisor's restart budget, and it never named the process actually holding the port.

## The real damage

Both spawn attempts happen **after** `writePidFile("supervisor")` and the failed child's `cleanupPidFile("server")`. So an instance that cannot bind overwrites the pid files of the healthy instance that *does* own the port:

- `supervisor/.pid` ends up pointing at the dead starter
- `server/.pid` is deleted outright

which de-registers a server that is up and serving. Observed live: healthy server `19348` under supervisor `11108`, while `supervisor/.pid` read `21440` (dead) and `server/.pid` was gone. `omniroute stop` still worked, but only by falling through to its `killByPort` port fallback rather than by the pid files.

## Fix

`serve` now resolves the port owner **before** spawning anything or touching a pid file:

```
✖ Port 20128 is already in use by PID 19348.
  Another OmniRoute is most likely already serving there, so open http://localhost:20128 before starting a second one.
  To replace it:    omniroute stop, then start again
  To run alongside: omniroute serve --port <other-port>
```

That is real output from the patched code run against an actual conflict.

Discovery is `findListeningPids()` in `bin/cli/utils/pid.mjs` — netstat on win32, lsof elsewhere. It mirrors `killByPort()`'s discovery in `stop.mjs`; consolidating the two is worth doing next time that file is touched, and is deliberately left out of this PR to keep `killByPort`'s injected-deps tests (#9455) untouched. A discovery failure reports the port as **free**, since a false "busy" would block a legitimate start, the worse of the two failures.

## Tests

New `tests/unit/cli-serve-port-in-use-preflight.test.mjs`, 6 cases: win32 netstat parsing (including that `TIME_WAIT` rows and other ports are ignored), posix lsof parsing, discovery failure treated as free, `reportPortInUse` naming the port/PID/remedies, and an end-to-end case that opens a real socket and asserts the preflight finds the owning process.

The `#2460` / `#6800` / `#11766` readiness guards still pass (6/6), since `pid.mjs` is shared.

title: fix(cli): escalate the readiness probe timeout so a slow health response is not a phantom boot failure
body:
## Problem

`omniroute serve` prints

```
⚠ Server did not respond within 60s. It may still be starting, or may have failed silently.
```

over a server that is **up and serving traffic**. In the reported case the process went on to
proxy real requests for the rest of the session; only the readiness signal timed out.

## Root cause

Every probe of `/api/monitoring/health` was aborted at a fixed `AbortSignal.timeout(2000)`, and a
timed-out probe is classified `"hanging"`, which `waitForServer` refuses to count toward readiness
(the #6800 guard). That puts a hard 2s ceiling on how slow a *healthy* first response is allowed to
be, and the poll cannot recover once it is crossed:

- the abort tears the socket down before the route finishes, so all of its work is discarded and
  the route's own 1s payload cache is never populated;
- 500ms later the next probe restarts the same work into the same 2s ceiling;
- repeat for the whole 60s budget.

A cold Windows boot crosses that ceiling easily: this route resolves ~10 dynamic imports and reads
the DB before it can answer. On an idle machine the first response measures ~2.5-4s.

Same failure family as #10508, which fixed it by taking a DNS lookup *out* of the 2s budget rather
than by widening the budget.

## Fix

- `bin/cli/utils/pid.mjs`: `pollHealthOnce` accepts a `probeTimeoutMs`, and `waitForServer`
  escalates it after each hang (2s, 4s, 8s, 15s), clamped to the time left in the budget so the
  caller's total timeout still holds. **Only a hang escalates**, so #6800's guarantee is unchanged:
  a socket that accepts TCP and never answers still resolves `false`.
- `waitForServer` reports each probe outcome to an optional `onOutcome` callback.
- `bin/cli/commands/serve.mjs`: the readiness-timeout diagnostic uses that outcome to say whether
  the port was accepting connections, separating "up and still warming up" from "never bound the
  port". That is the line that makes this failure diagnosable instead of alarming.

## Tests

New `tests/unit/waitForServer-slow-first-response.test.mjs`:

1. a health route answering 200 in 3.2s is reported ready (**fails on `main`**: the old poller ran
   12 probes over 30s and returned `ready=false` every time);
2. escalation stays clamped to the caller's budget (a never-answering socket with an 8s budget
   returns `false` in ~8.5s, not ~10s+);
3. the timeout diagnostic distinguishes a listening port from a dead one.

Existing guards all still pass (`cli-waitForServer.test.mjs`, `waitForServer-tcp-fallback-6800.test.mjs`):
#2460, #6800 and #11766, 9/9 green. The #10508 source-text guard is unaffected (host list and fetch
template unchanged).

End to end against a real install, the patched poller reports ready in 3.9s with the probe trace
`not-listening -> hanging -> ready`; the escalated second probe is what catches it.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The CLI polls the **heavy** `/api/monitoring/health` every 500ms, whose own docstring points
high-frequency pollers at `/api/health/ping` instead, and that is exactly what the Electron
readiness poller (`electron/lib/serverReadiness.js`) already uses. Switching the CLI probe route
would remove the cost that creates this ceiling, but it changes the readiness contract and the
#10508 guard, so it is left as a separate change.

title: fix(vertex): discover and route partner models correctly
body:
## Summary

- support both Vertex API keys and Service Account JSON credentials without mixing their capabilities
- infer and persist the Google Cloud consumer project for project-scoped API-key partner inference
- use API-key model discovery only for Gemini and fall back intentionally to a curated project-scoped catalog because Google rejects API keys for publishers.models.list
- fetch the live Model Garden catalog for Google, xAI, Anthropic, Mistral, and open-MaaS publishers with OAuth or Service Account credentials using Google's maximum page size of 300
- treat the authenticated Google publisher catalog as the live source for current Gemini chat models, including Gemini 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, and 3.8 Flash
- retain successful publisher results when the separate Gemini Developer API rejects Service Accounts
- accept requestAccess-backed MaaS model cards while excluding image, TTS, live, transcription, embedding, OCR-only, and retired Gemini entries from the chat catalog
- replace invalid speculative Vertex IDs with documented MaaS IDs such as deepseek-ai/deepseek-v3.2-maas, qwen/qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct-maas, and zai-org/glm-5-maas
- route Gemini, Anthropic, Mistral, xAI, and generic OpenAI-compatible MaaS publishers through their correct transports
- label the dashboard credential field accurately and explain that Service Account JSON enables live Model Garden discovery
- reject OAuth client configuration JSON with a specific explanation instead of reporting missing Service Account fields

## Authentication behavior

A project-bound API key can execute partner models, but Google does not allow it to call Model Garden publishers.models.list. OmniRoute extracts the bound project from structured Google error metadata and uses the curated project-scoped catalog.

A Service Account JSON credential is exchanged for an OAuth access token. That bearer token can list publishers/google/models and the partner publisher catalogs, so successful discovery now returns catalogMode=live_vertex_catalog without supplementing the result with a stale static Gemini baseline.

Google separately rejects Service Accounts on generativelanguage.googleapis.com. That expected rejection no longer marks the entire Vertex discovery as failed.

An OAuth web-client JSON file is only client configuration and is not itself an access credential. It requires a complete authorization-code and refresh-token flow and is now rejected with a clear message.

## Reproduction covered

The live Publisher Model list request used pageSize=1000 although Google enforces a maximum of 300. Every publisher returned HTTP 400, leaving an empty discovery result and causing Sync Models to report:

Vertex model catalogs unavailable — using local catalog

The corrected request returns the live Google and partner catalogs. Gemini chat filtering is capability-oriented: current Flash/Flash Lite/Pro variants from Gemini 2.5 onward are imported, while non-chat and retired entries are excluded.

- focused provider-dialog tests from the credential UI change: 20 passed

- deployed live catalog includes gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.7-flash, gemini-3.8-flash, claude-opus-4-1, and mistral-medium-3

title: feat(sse): add LLM Gateway DevPass quota tracking
body:
## Summary

Adds DevPass quota tracking for the **`llmgateway`** provider, so the LLM Gateway subscription allowance shows up in OmniRoute's quota telemetry (Dashboard → Limits, quota-aware preflight/monitor) alongside OpenRouter, OpenCode, etc.

LLM Gateway exposes a single documented endpoint — [`GET /v1/key`](https://docs.llmgateway.io/developers/devpass-usage) — authenticated with the connection's own gateway API key (`llmgtwy_…`). It returns the DevPass allowance as decimal-string USD values. This PR mirrors the existing `openrouterQuotaFetcher.ts` API-key pattern.

## What it surfaces

Two independent DevPass windows:
- **Monthly plan credits** — `devPlanCreditsUsed` / `devPlanCreditsLimit` / `devPlanCreditsRemaining` (the recurring DevPass allowance).
- **Weekly premium-model window** — `devPlanPremiumWeeklyLimit` / `devPlanPremiumCreditsUsed` / `devPlanPremiumWeekResetsAt` (7-day rolling; resets to full allowance when the window expires).

Edge cases handled (per the upstream docs):
- All USD values are decimal **strings** → parsed before math.
- Pay-as-you-go keys (`devPlan: "none"`) return no quota (treated as unlimited).
- `401` (invalid/inactive key) and `403` (publishable/session key) fail open — quota tracking never blocks routing.
- 45s TTL cache keyed by connectionId, so combo preflight/monitor polling doesn't hammer the endpoint.

## Changes

- **`open-sse/services/llmgatewayQuotaFetcher.ts`** (new) — fetch + parse `/v1/key`, build a `QuotaInfo` with monthly + weekly premium windows, cache, and `registerLlmgatewayQuotaFetcher()`.
- **`open-sse/services/usage/llmgateway.ts`** (new) — dashboard usage leaf returning the two `UsageQuota` rows.
- **`src/sse/handlers/chat.ts`** — register the bespoke fetcher before `registerGenericQuotaFetchers()` (so it wins over the generic path) + its named windows.
- **`open-sse/services/usage.ts`** + **`usage/fetcherProviders.ts`** — dispatch case + registration list entry.
- **`open-sse/services/usage/supportedProviders.ts`** + **`src/lib/usage/providerLimits.ts`** — add `llmgateway` to `USAGE_SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS` and `PROVIDER_LIMITS_APIKEY_PROVIDERS` (otherwise `/api/usage/[connectionId]` rejects the connection).
- **`ProviderLimits/constants.ts`** — dashboard label + order.
- **`tests/unit/llmgateway-quota-fetcher.test.ts`** (new) — 21 cases.

## Testing

- `tests/unit/llmgateway-quota-fetcher.test.ts` — **21/21 pass** (parser incl. decimal strings + expired premium window; 401/403/network fail-open; pay-as-you-go → null; cache TTL; monthly & weekly exhaustion → `limitReached`; registration wires preflight/monitor/windows; preflight proceed vs block; usage leaf rows).
- Regression: `generic-quota-fetcher` (10/10), `provider-limits-ui` (25/25), `free-tier-providers-wave1-c` (2/2) still green — bespoke registration doesn't disturb the generic ordering.
- `npm run typecheck:core` clean.
- New files lint-clean; `check:provider-consistency` OK.

title: fix(perplexity-web): preserve system contract on follow-up requests
body:
**Summary**
This PR addresses the OmniRoute-side bug described in #12104 where follow-up messages on the `perplexity-web` provider drop the system instructions containing the injected tool-use contract, causing subsequent conversational turns to fail at using tools.

**Root Cause**
When formatting a follow-up request, `buildQuery()` historically hit an early return if a `followUpUuid` was present, returning only `parsed.currentMsg` and explicitly discarding the `systemMsg` instruction block.

**Proposed Solution**
Updated `buildQuery` to correctly prepend `parsed.systemMsg` (and the `SEARCH_HINT`, if enabled) to `parsed.currentMsg` when formatting follow-up requests. This preserves the injected instructions for the lifetime of the session without interfering with the existing UI abstraction.

**Important Clarification**
This PR **only** fixes OmniRoute's explicit dropping of instructions for follow-up turns. It **does not** claim to fix upstream limitations in Perplexity's own backend where their model might refuse or mangle structured JSON during its first response. This ensures the contract is successfully sent; how the backend handles it remains upstream behavior.

**Notes for Reviewers**
- A regression test (`tests/unit/12104-perplexity-web-followup-contract.test.ts`) is included to verify that `buildQuery` correctly includes the system contract strings on Turn 2+ follow-ups.

title: fix(perplexity-web): declare tool-calling params unsupported
body:
**Summary**
This PR fixes an issue where providing tool schemas to a combo/auto route that falls back to `perplexity-web` results in an immediate 400 error. 

**Root Cause**
The `perplexity-web` registry configuration lacked the explicit `unsupportedParams` metadata array. As a result, OmniRoute's `chatCore` failed to recognize that the provider cannot process tool parameters.

**Proposed Solution**
Added `unsupportedParams: ["tools", "tool_choice", "parallel_tool_calls"]` to the `perplexity-web` registry entry. 
- On direct requests, this triggers `stripUnsupportedParams`, correctly sanitizing the payload before execution.
- On auto/combo fallback, it triggers `filterTargetsByRequestCompatibility`, ensuring requests requiring tool calling don't route to this unsupported backend.

**Notes for Reviewers**
- This aligns `perplexity-web` with the standard API `pplx-*` models which already declare tool calling as unsupported.
- This change strictly affects capability routing and sanitization prior to execution. It does not modify the `perplexity-web` executor protocol itself.
- A regression test (`tests/unit/12104-perplexity-web-tools-unsupported.test.ts`) is included to verify the compatibility logic integration.

title: fix(chatCore): stop executeWithUpstreamStartTimeout leaking its abortPromise listener (hedge-cancelled process exit)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the `Error [AbortError]: hedge-cancelled` process exit (exit code 7) seen on a production instance on 2026-08-31, and hardens the process crash guard around it.

**Root cause** (mapped from the built chunks back to source and reproduced): `executeWithUpstreamStartTimeout` in `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/upstreamTimeouts.ts` registered a `{ once: true }` abort listener for `abortPromise` on the long-lived client/stream signal and never removed it in `finally`, so every executor attempt (and every retry) leaked one listener. `Promise.race` only subscribes once the array literal has been evaluated; when `execute()` threw synchronously the race never ran, `abortPromise` was orphaned, and the next hedge cancellation / client disconnect aborted the signal with the string reason that `streamHandler.ts` forwards. `createAbortError()` rebuilt it as an `AbortError`-named Error and rejected a promise nothing awaited. That `unhandledRejection` reached `src/shared/utils/httpClientAbortGuard.mjs`, whose handler re-threw it as an `uncaughtException`, and the process exited.

## Commits

1. `fix(sse): stop mergeAbortSignals from leaking abort listeners` - the listener-hygiene change from #12391 (`open-sse/executors/base.ts`), included so this branch is self-contained. Note: that change is correct but is **not** on the crash path above.
2. `fix(server): stop the crash guard re-throwing combo abort reasons` - `isClientAbortError()` now absorbs `AbortError`s and the combo abort reasons from `comboAbortReasons.ts` (`hedge-cancelled`, `combo-per-model-timeout`). Ports the upstream guard tests and makes the child-process tests Windows-portable (a `file://` URL instead of a bare path in dynamic `import()`).
3. `fix(chatCore): stop executeWithUpstreamStartTimeout leaking its abortPromise listener` - the root-cause fix: keep a handle to the listener and remove it with the others in `finally`; mark the two race-loser promises as handled so a synchronous throw from `execute()` can never orphan them. Race semantics are unchanged.
4. `fix(server): absorb raw string abort reasons in the crash guard; document the verified crash path` - `streamHandler.ts` aborts with raw string reasons and undici rejects with `signal.reason` verbatim, so a cancellation can reach process level as a bare string; the guard now absorbs those too. Comments corrected to describe the verified mechanism.

## Tests

- New regression tests in `tests/unit/chatcore-upstream-timeouts.test.ts` (+2; both fail against the previous implementation: one asserts no listener growth after a resolving `execute`, one asserts that a synchronously throwing `execute` followed by a late `hedge-cancelled` abort produces no `unhandledRejection`).
- `tests/unit/httpClientAbortGuard.test.mjs` (+9), including a real child-process replay of the production shape on both the `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` routes, and a genuine-error case that must still crash.
- Results: `httpClientAbortGuard` 18/18, `chatcore-upstream-timeouts` 7/7, `executor-base-utils` 23/23; 127 related unit test files 968/970 (the 2 failures reproduce identically on the base commit: a stale G13 golden and a Windows temp-dir EPERM on cleanup).
- `tsc --noEmit -p open-sse/tsconfig.json` clean; eslint clean on the changed files.

## Related

- Extends #12391, which on its own does not fix the exit.
- Separately observed on Windows and not addressed here: `scripts/build/bootstrap-env.mjs` resolves `DATA_DIR` to `%APPDATA%\omniroute` while `src/lib/dataPaths.ts` prefers a legacy `~/.omniroute` when it exists, so the first `npm start` of a source checkout can auto-generate a new `STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and orphan every previously encrypted credential. Happy to file it as an issue.

title: feat(deploy): Kubernetes support for k3s and k8s
body:
## Summary

The repo ships `docker-compose.yml` and `fly.toml`, and `DOCKER_GUIDE.md` already warns that "stock Docker / Kubernetes OmniRoute is one Node process + one SQLite writer" — but there are no manifests. Anyone running this on k3s or k8s writes them from scratch, against a topology whose constraints are invisible until they bite:

- a second replica against the same volume corrupts the database;
- an ingress that buffers responses withholds the SSE stream until the provider turn ends, which reads as a hung request, not as broken streaming;
- a liveness probe pointed at `/api/monitoring/health` does real DB work on every kubelet tick and restarts the only pod under load.

So the topology is **encoded, not documented**. `replicas: 1`, `Recreate` and `ReadWriteOnce` are fixed in the base, in the chart and in the generator — not exposed as options anywhere. And the chart and the spec schema refuse to render a configuration that fails at runtime, naming the field rather than emitting something that breaks later:

| Rejected | Because |
| --- | --- |
| `replicaCount > 1` | two pods on one volume corrupt the SQLite file |
| access mode ≠ `ReadWriteOnce` | a shared-write volume invites the same second writer |
| heap ceiling ≥ memory limit | the kernel OOM-kills the pod instead of Node raising a recoverable heap error (#7849) |
| `shutdownTimeoutMs` ≥ grace − preStop | the kubelet SIGKILLs mid-drain, so in-flight SSE is cut rather than drained |
| TLS with no Ingress | terminating TLS at something that does not exist |

Four artifacts, one topology:

- **`deploy/kubernetes/`** — Kustomize base plus k3s (Traefik + `local-path`) and generic k8s (ingress-nginx) overlays.
- **`deploy/helm/omniroute/`** — the same topology, values-driven.
- **`omniroute deploy k8s`** — prints manifests built from a running instance's settings, so ports, origins and flags are not transcribed by hand. It writes to stdout and touches nothing, so it composes: `omniroute deploy k8s --target local | kubectl apply -f -`.
- **`docs/ops/KUBERNETES_DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md`** — 416 lines covering deploy, ingress/SSE, probes, upgrades, storage/backups, sizing and troubleshooting.

`local` and `vps` differ only in defaults. `local` assumes k3s on the same machine. `vps` assumes a hostname in front of a cluster other people can reach, so TLS is on, `REQUIRE_API_KEY=true`, the cluster's default StorageClass binds, and `LIVE_WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is derived from the host — without that, the dashboard's live view is rejected by the origin check on the very host it is served from.

Probes follow `docs/ops/MONITORING_GUIDE.md` ("Kubernetes probe recommendations", merged in #10297): `/healthz` for startup and readiness, `/livez` for liveness, never `/api/monitoring/health`. The nginx overlay disables response buffering; the Traefik idle-timeout caveat is documented for k3s, since that one is an entrypoint setting and not an Ingress annotation.

**Provisioning is advisory on purpose.** `omniroute deploy k8s provision` prints the k3s commands and never runs them or connects to a server. Doing it directly would mean shipping an SSH client and holding a private key — a standing surface for a one-off task — so it follows the shape `contrib/vps` already uses for a VPS install. The VPS plan covers the two steps easiest to get wrong by hand: `--tls-san`, without which the cluster is only reachable as `127.0.0.1` and a remote `kubectl` fails TLS verification, and rewriting the `127.0.0.1` server address in the kubeconfig k3s writes. Values rendered into those commands are constrained to hostname, version, username and context shapes, so a printed command cannot mean something other than what it looks like.

**No new API route and no new dashboard surface.** An earlier draft put this behind `/api/deploy/*` with a UI tab; it was dropped before landing. Applying manifests by clicking is at odds with GitOps — the desired state should be versioned, not produced by a form — and the routes existed only to serve the button, spawning `kubectl` with the host kubeconfig, which is a full cluster credential. The CLI reaches the same result without that surface, so `routeGuard.ts` is untouched.

**Two fixes to the manifests themselves**, both surfaced by the test that pins the generator against `deploy/kubernetes/base`:

- Dropped `API_PORT` from the base ConfigMap. Setting it moves the API to a separate port (`src/lib/runtime/ports.ts:27`) that neither the container nor the Service exposes, leaving that listener unreachable. Unset, the API and dashboard share `PORT` — which is what the manifests actually expose.
- Made the container port protocol explicit, so the committed manifest and the generator agree byte for byte.

`deploy` also joins `--mcp` in reserving stdout for data (`bin/omniroute.mjs`). Env-loading notices there made the YAML unparseable — `control characters are not allowed` — which broke the pipe the command exists for.

## Related Issues

- Related to #10297 — the probe recommendations these manifests implement
- Related to #7849 — the V8-heap-vs-cgroup ceiling the spec schema now enforces
- Related to #8075 — multi-writer HA; until it ships, single-replica is the documented ceiling and this PR encodes it

## Validation

- [x] Change type: build-deploy (plus CLI)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

**Applied to a live cluster, not just a dry run.** Single-node k3s v1.36.4+k3s1:

| Checked | Result |
| --- | --- |
| PVC on `local-path` | `Bound`, 10Gi, RWO |
| Pod | `1/1 Running`, 0 restarts |
| Rollout | completed, `Available=True` |
| `/healthz` and `/livez` through the Service | HTTP 200 both |
| `/v1/models` | answers application JSON, so the app serves — not just the probes |
| Probe failure events | none recorded |
| Helm chart, `--dry-run=server` | accepted by the real API server |

That run corrected two documentation errors a client-side dry run cannot catch: the health check used `wget`, and the published image ships neither `wget` nor `curl` (`node` is the only HTTP client in it); and an Ingress naming an IngressClass the cluster does not run is accepted by the API server and then silently routes nothing. Both are now in the guide, the second as a troubleshooting row.

Red first, per invariant: each manifest guard was verified to fail under a deliberate mutation of the file it protects — flipping `replicas` to 2, the access mode to RWX, `proxy-buffering` to `on`, liveness to `/api/monitoring/health`, or the shutdown budget past the grace period each turns exactly one test red, and only one. The generator/CLI suites found three real defects while being written: a `fail` placed at the top level of a `_*.tpl` file (Helm parses and discards it, so the replica guard was a silent no-op), context-name validation that rejected legitimate EKS contexts, and the stdout pollution above.

The automated review then found four more, fixed in the second commit: an address pattern that accepted a port or a bare IPv6 literal and rendered `https://host:123:6443`; a context pattern that rejected the ARN-shaped contexts managed clusters produce; the context being interpolated into a temp path, which the previous item would have turned into a directory traversal; and a quantity pattern that accepted `K` while rejecting `k`, the lowercase decimal thousand Kubernetes actually uses, so `512k` was refused. Each has a regression case.

Rebased onto `release/v3.8.51` and the full set rerun there: **54 tests passing**, `npm run typecheck:core` clean, both overlays render with zero kustomize warnings, `helm lint` clean, `check:docs-all` / `check:tracked-artifacts` / `check:cli-i18n` passing, and `omniroute deploy k8s | kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f -` still creates all six objects.

`npm run lint` reports **zero errors** but exits 2, on this branch and on an untouched checkout of the base alike — `suppressions left that do not occur anymore`, unrelated to any file here.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/k8s-deploy-manifests.test.ts` — 12 cases over the committed manifests: single replica, Recreate, RWO, probe targets, drain budget, unbuffered SSE, secret hygiene, and that the chart's replica guard is actually reachable rather than discarded.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-manifest-generator.test.ts` — 13 cases: generation invariants, target profiles, storage-class semantics, and parity between the generator and `deploy/kubernetes/base`.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-provision-plan.test.ts` — 19 cases: the provisioning plan's correctness (including `--tls-san` and the kubeconfig rewrite), the deploy-spec guard rails, and the five review findings below.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-cli-command.test.ts` — 10 cases driving the real binary: the stdout contract, exit codes, and argument rejection.

## Coverage Notes

New production code is `src/lib/deploy/kubernetes/` (three pure modules, 830 lines) and `bin/cli/commands/deploy.mjs` (250 lines).

The generator and the spec schema are pure — no cluster, no filesystem, no clock — and are covered directly by the two unit suites. The CLI is covered end to end by a suite that executes `bin/omniroute.mjs` and parses its stdout, which is what pinned the stdout-pollution bug; a mocked test would not have caught it. `bin/omniroute.mjs` gains one condition, exercised by that same suite.

Nothing existing loses coverage. Beyond the new files, the only changes are the two ConfigMap/protocol fixes, that one condition, a `.prettierignore` entry for Helm's Go templates (which Prettier's YAML parser cannot read), and two doc cross-references.

## Reviewer Notes

- **The chart's guard rails live in a `define` that `deployment.yaml` includes.** Helm parses and then discards top-level code in a `_*.tpl` file, so a bare `fail` there is a silent no-op — the first version of this had exactly that bug, and `replicaCount=2` rendered happily. A test now pins the `include`.
- **`storageClassName` is omitted, never set to `""`.** An empty string disables dynamic provisioning entirely; omitting the key binds the cluster default. The two look interchangeable, so a test covers the distinction.
- **The k3s overlay assumes the Traefik that k3s ships by default.** A cluster installed with `--disable=traefik` has no such IngressClass, and the API server accepts the Ingress anyway — it is created and routes nothing. Documented in troubleshooting rather than worked around, since the fix is to name the class the cluster actually runs.
- **Context names accept `:` and `/`.** Managed clusters produce them (an EKS context is `arn:aws:eks:<region>:<account>:cluster/<name>`). Safe because nothing here goes through a shell, the leading-alphanumeric requirement prevents a value being read as an *option*, and — the part that had to change for this to hold — the temp filename in the fetch-kubeconfig step is fixed rather than derived from the context, so a `/` cannot turn it into a path.
- **Recreate means every upgrade is a short full outage** — in-flight SSE and dashboard sessions drop, and the empty-endpoint window returns a controller `502`. That is the SQLite topology, not a probe misconfiguration, and the guide says so where an operator will hit it.
- The `--tls-san` step matters more than it looks: omit it and the cluster works perfectly from the VPS itself while every remote `kubectl` fails TLS verification, which is a confusing way to lose an afternoon.
- No migration, no feature flag, no change to the request path, no new environment variable.

title: fix(sse): stop mergeAbortSignals from leaking abort listeners
body:
## Summary

`mergeAbortSignals()` in `open-sse/executors/base.ts` attached `"abort"` listeners to its `primary`/`secondary` signals but never removed them once the merged signal settled. Every executor fetch attempt calls this (`fetchWithStartTimeout`, once per URL/retry), so a busy combo request accumulated one live listener per call on the long-lived combo/client signal. A leaked listener still fires when that signal is later aborted (e.g. a hedge cancellation arriving after this merge's own caller already finished), for a merged output nothing is watching anymore.

Fix mirrors the already-correct self-cleaning pattern in `open-sse/utils/directResponseStartTimeout.ts`'s local `mergeAbortSignals`.

Originally investigated from a production crash: `Error [AbortError]: hedge-cancelled` thrown unhandled from deep inside the built Next.js server bundle, killing the whole Node process. This fix addresses one confirmed, measured listener leak on the exact signal-merge path that carries the hedge-cancellation reason through every provider fetch — it removes a real defect regardless, though it was not possible to build a full end-to-end repro of that exact crash through the entire combo-hedging dispatch path.

## Test plan

- [x] TDD: added a regression test (`tests/unit/executor-base-utils.test.ts`) that merges the same long-lived signal 25 times and counts real listener growth via `node:events`' `getEventListeners`.
- [x] Confirmed red on pre-fix code: exactly 25 leaked listeners after 25 merges.
- [x] Confirmed green on fixed code: 0 leaked listeners, 23/23 tests passing in the full file.
- [x] Ran `tests/unit/executor-base-utils.test.ts` on Windows (the platform the original crash was observed on) — 23/23 pass.
- [x] Scoped ESLint on both changed files — 0 new violations (pre-existing violations elsewhere in `base.ts` are outside this diff's hunks).

title: fix(pack): include BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH in APP_STAGING_ALLOWED_EXACT_PATHS
body:
## Summary

Sentinel written by `write-build-base-path.mjs` into the standalone dist/ directory. Consumed at container start by `ensure-docker-base-path.mjs` to compare the baked-in `OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH` against the runtime value.

Without this entry, prepublish Step 10.7 (`findUnexpectedArtifactPaths`) prunes `dist/BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH` as an unexpected artifact before the tarball is packaged. The Docker container then crashes at startup with a missing sentinel (same class as the `BUILD_SHA` / #7065 incident).

## Fix

Added `"BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH"` to `APP_STAGING_ALLOWED_EXACT_PATHS` in `scripts/build/pack-artifact-policy.ts`.

## Verification

- `git diff scripts/build/pack-artifact-policy.ts` confirms the single-line addition
- No test file changes required: the fix is a pure allowlist addition
- Pre-existing typecheck errors in `tray.ts`, `responsesTransformer.ts` etc. are unrelated to this change

## Regression testing

After merging, verify the standalone `npm pack` output contains `BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH`:
```bash
npm run build:release
npm pack
tar -tf omniroute-*.tgz | grep BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH
```
Expected: `package/dist/BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH`

title: fix(memory): word/sentence-boundary aware fact truncation
body:
## Bug

`src/lib/memory/extraction.ts` truncates extracted memory facts with raw
character-offset slicing and no boundary awareness:

- `sanitizeMatch()` did `raw.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, MAX_FACT_LENGTH)`
  — a hard cut that can land mid-word.
- `capExtractionText()` did `text.slice(-MAX_EXTRACTION_TEXT_LENGTH)` on the
  front edge when input exceeds `MAX_EXTRACTION_TEXT_LENGTH` (64KB) — same
  problem, opposite edge.

These facts later get injected into LLM context as `<system-reminder>`
memory blocks, so a mid-word/mid-clause cut produces garbled fragments
(e.g. text starting with a stray closing parenthesis, or ending with no
punctuation and a half word).

## Fix

- `sanitizeMatch()` now backs the cut index off to the nearest clean
  boundary within a lookback window: prefers a sentence-ending mark
  (`.`/`!`/`?`) so the fact reads as a complete clause, falls back to a
  plain whitespace/word boundary, and only falls back to the original hard
  cut when no boundary exists in the window (e.g. one long unbroken run of
  characters).
- `capExtractionText()` applies the equivalent boundary-aware trim on the
  front edge of the kept tail (extends the cut forward to the next
  whitespace boundary rather than slicing mid-word).

This mirrors the boundary-aware truncation already used by
`open-sse/services/compression/lite.ts` (issue #8169) for tool-result
truncation, so the codebase now has one consistent pattern for this class
of problem.

## Testing

- New: `tests/unit/memory-extraction-boundary-truncation.test.ts` — covers
  a long match cut at a word boundary, a match cut preferentially at
  sentence-ending punctuation, short strings passing through untouched,
  the no-boundary-in-window fallback, and `capExtractionText`'s
  boundary-aware tail behavior (both under and over the 64KB cap).
- Ran existing `tests/unit/memory-extraction.test.ts` alongside the new
  file — all 28 tests pass, no regressions:
  ```
  ℹ tests 28
  ℹ pass 28
  ℹ fail 0
  ```
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — no new type errors introduced by
  this change.

No unrelated files were touched.

title: fix(sse): stop CircuitBreaker.execute() from counting a resolved upstream failure as a success
body:
⚠️ base-red inherited: #12335

## Summary

Fixes #12254. `CircuitBreaker.execute()` calls `_onSuccess()` for any non-throwing resolution of
`fn()`, but `handleChatCore()` returns `{success:false, status:5xx}` for ordinary upstream failures
without throwing. `executeChatWithBreaker`'s `breaker.execute(chatFn)` therefore called
`_onSuccess()` on every dispatch through this call site regardless of outcome — and in CLOSED
state `_onSuccess()` does `failureCount = Math.max(0, failureCount - 1)`, which silently cancelled
the very next explicit `_onFailure()` call in `chat.ts` / `accountFallback.ts` for the same
attempt. `failureCount` could never climb past ~1, so the provider breaker could never open under
sustained genuine failures — on both the direct dispatch path and the combo path (same
per-provider breaker singleton via `getCircuitBreaker(provider)`).

## Fix

Adds `CircuitBreaker.executeTrackingFailureOnly()`: identical `OPEN`/`HALF_OPEN` gating and
identical `isFailure`/`classifyError`-based failure accounting on an actual throw, but it never
calls `_onSuccess()` just because `fn()` resolved. Success/failure accounting for a *resolved*
result stays exactly where it already lives — the explicit `_onSuccess()`/`_onFailure()` call
sites in `chat.ts` and `recordProviderSuccess()`/`recordProviderFailure()` in
`accountFallback.ts` (the combo path already uses these explicitly, per `combo.ts:2358/1870/3587`
gated by `shouldRecordProviderBreakerFailure()`). `executeChatWithBreaker`'s two
`breaker.execute()` call sites are switched to the new method. `CircuitBreaker.execute()` itself
is untouched — it has no other callers in the codebase.

This is the direction discussed in #12254: a shared classification
(`PROVIDER_BREAKER_FAILURE_STATUSES` / `shouldRecordProviderBreakerFailure`) already exists on the
combo side and the single-model side already does explicit `_onFailure()`/`_onSuccess()` calls —
the one remaining gap was this single `execute()` call site quietly fighting all of that explicit
accounting.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/circuit-breaker-provider-accounting-12254.test.ts` — unit tests on `CircuitBreaker`
  directly: no implicit accounting on a resolved (non-throwing) call; failure accounting on an
  actual throw still honors `classifyError`; consecutive genuine failures escalate to `OPEN`
  without being cancelled by interleaved non-throwing calls (the exact reported bug shape); `OPEN`
  and `HALF_OPEN` gating unchanged.
- `tests/unit/execute-chat-with-breaker-accounting-12254.test.ts` — end-to-end reproduction at the
  actual regressed call site: drives 6 real upstream 502s through `executeChatWithBreaker` (mocked
  `global.fetch`, same harness pattern as `execute-chat-resource-pressure-breaker.test.ts`) and
  asserts the breaker accumulates zero implicit accounting.

Ran locally: `npm run typecheck:core` (clean), `npm run lint` (clean), `npm run check:cycles`
(clean), plus the full existing circuit-breaker/combo-provider-cooldown/account-fallback test
files (174 tests, all passing) to confirm no regression from the new method or the two swapped
call sites.

## Changelog

Fragment to follow in this same branch once the PR number is known (`changelog.d/README.md`
convention).

title: fix(combo): scope Claude model failures to the model, not the account
body:
## Summary

A priority combo whose steps are five different models on one Claude OAuth connection stops at step 1: whatever kills the first step is recorded against the connection, and the pre-dispatch cooldown gate then skips every later step because they share that connection. The drop order is silently a single-model route.

`hasPerModelQuota()` returns false for `claude`, so in `markAccountUnavailable()` the model-lockout branch never runs and the failure lands on the connection row instead. `getPersistedConnectionCooldownSkipReason()` takes it from there.

To keep the model-specific bug in #12334 out of the picture, I reproduced it with a first step naming a model that cannot exist. The 404 lands and step 2 is never dispatched; point step 2 at a different account and the same combo works:

```
COMBO: Trying model 1/2: claude/claude-bogus-model-x
COMBO: All models failed | claude/claude-bogus-model-x: model — model: claude-bogus-model-x (HTTP 404)
COMBO: Trying model 2/2: agy/claude-sonnet-4-6      ← only when step 2 is another account
```

A Claude OAuth connection multiplexes Fable 5, Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet and Haiku behind one credential — the multiplexing the doc comment on `hasPerModelQuota` already describes. Its quota is a different question, though: a 429 on a Max subscription is account-wide, and `shouldMarkAccountExhaustedFrom429("claude", …)` pins that in `account-fallback-service.test.ts`. Adding `claude` to `hasPerModelQuota` breaks that test, and rightly so.

So this splits the two: a new `hasPerModelFailureScope()` covers the non-quota statuses (404, 5xx, a stream that ended with no content), `auth.ts` uses it only when `status !== 429`, and quota scope stays exactly as it was. `targetExhaustion` gets the same treatment for 404, which names one model the account cannot serve rather than a bad connection — the empty-content 502 was already exempt through `isEmptyContentFailure`.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12334

## Validation

- [x] Change type: routing
- [x] Focused tests: `tests/unit/combo-claude-per-model-scope.test.ts` plus every existing test touching `hasPerModelQuota` or `targetExhaustion` — 17 files, 226 passing, 0 failing
- [x] `npx eslint` on the four touched files: same 3 pre-existing `no-unused-vars` errors in `accountFallback.ts` before and after (line 2413 shifts to 2437), no new ones
- [x] Reconciled with `release/v3.8.51`
- [x] Production-code changes come with a new test

Full unit suite on this branch: 47 failures. On the same checkout with the patch stashed: 46. The one extra is `Vietnamese locale has no internal missing markers or empty fallbacks`, which fails on a clean tree when run on its own:

```
not ok 1 - Vietnamese locale has complete key parity with English
not ok 2 - Vietnamese locale has no internal missing markers or empty fallbacks
```

so it is suite variance, not this change.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/combo-claude-per-model-scope.test.ts` (new) — mirrors `combo-provider-cooldown-sibling.test.ts`: failure scope for `claude`, quota scope unchanged, the connection-level override still winning, and the two sides of the pre-dispatch gate (a real cooldown still protects siblings; no cooldown lets step 2 dispatch).

## Coverage Notes

`hasPerModelFailureScope()` is covered by the new file. The `auth.ts` and `targetExhaustion.ts` call sites are covered indirectly by the existing lockout tests for gemini, github, nvidia, ollama, openrouter, vertex and agentrouter, which all still pass — they pin that nothing outside `claude` changed scope.

## Reviewer Notes

The risk worth looking at is the 429 split. title: feat(perf): lazy-boot quota auto-ping scheduler + build heap floor guard
body:
## Summary

Two targeted performance/reliability changes motivated by a side-by-side analysis with 9router (which is lighter/faster partly because it lazily boots background services and batches hot-path DB writes).

### 1. Lazy-boot the quota auto-ping scheduler (9router 27b37705 parity)

- `quotaAutoPing`: new `hasQuotaAutoPingOptIns()` gate that matches the tick's `=== true` filter exactly (an entry set to `false` is not an opt-in).
- `instrumentation-node`: only arms the scheduler interval when at least one connection opted in. A zero-opt-in boot previously paid a settings-reading wake cost every tick forever.
- `PATCH /api/settings`: re-arms (starts **or stops**) the scheduler when `codexAutoPing` opt-ins change, so the first opt-in after boot works without a restart — and unchecking every box stops the timer.

### 2. Build heap floor guard in `build-next-isolated.mjs`

An operator shell that exports `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=1024"` (a common dotfile leftover) was silently **respected** by the previous `\!/--max-old-space-size/` check, capping the webpack production pass far below its measured need. Measured on 2026-09-01 (16 GB macOS host):

| Scenario | Heap ceiling | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| inherited 1024 (dotfile case) | ~1 GB | OOM (SIGABRT) 12 s into compile |
| direct 2048 | ~2 GB | OOM at 2 GB heap, peak RSS 2469 MB |
| backend-only + 3072 | ~3 GB | OOM, heap fully consumed (Scavenge at 3021 MB) |
| full build | 4 GB floor (new behavior) | passes (validated below) |

The guard now **replaces in place** any inherited ceiling below the 4096 MB floor (no duplicate flags, unrelated NODE_OPTIONS entries preserved). `OMNIROUTE_BUILD_MEMORY_MB` overrides and inherited values ≥ floor remain respected, and Turbopack-native memory behavior is unchanged (see #6409).

## Tests

- `tests/unit/build-next-isolated.test.ts`: 12/12 pass (2 new: floor-replace semantics + unrelated-flag preservation)
- `tests/unit/quota-auto-ping.test.ts`: 20/20 pass (1 new: opt-in gate shapes incl. absent/empty/false entries)
