title: fix(providers): Vertex Express-key discovery failure is an intentional local-catalog fallback, not degraded (#12328)
body:
## What

Fixes #12328.

Vertex model discovery with a **Vertex AI Express API key** (`?key=` on `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models`) always fails with `400 API_KEY_INVALID` — the Generative Language API is a different service and does not accept Vertex-scoped keys. Today that failure falls back to the generic `API unavailable — using local catalog`, which reads as a transient/auth problem and sends users chasing key/permission ghosts, while the connection test and inference both succeed.

## Change

On discovery failure with `400/403` **and** an Express key (`queryKey` path, non-JSON credential):

- the fallback warning now names the real cause (`Vertex Express API key cannot list models on the Generative Language API (API_KEY_INVALID) — …`);
- the local catalog is served as an **intentional** source (`localIntentional`, #5460/#5465) so model-sync imports it instead of treating the response as a degraded remote fetch.

Everything else is untouched:

- SA-JSON (Bearer) discovery unchanged — live listing still parsed when it succeeds;
- transient errors (500, network, redirect-block) keep the existing generic fallback;
- the fetch attempt itself still happens (best effort; no capability removed for keys that *do* work on that endpoint).

## Test plan

New regression suite `tests/unit/vertex-express-discovery-12328.test.ts` (4 tests, real tmpdir DB + mocked `fetch`, same pattern as `7993-noauth-proxy-routing`):

1. Express key + 400 → 200, `source: local_catalog`, `intentional: true`, warning matches `API_KEY_INVALID`; exactly one call to the GL endpoint with `key=` in query;
2. Express key + 403 → same intentional fallback;
3. Express key + 500 → generic fallback, **not** intentional, no `API_KEY_INVALID` in warning (no behavior change);
4. SA-JSON (real RSA key generated in-test; `importPKCS8` rejects placeholders) → OAuth token mocked, live GL list parsed, `source: api`, no `?key=` on the wire.

Local verification on `release/v3.8.51`:

```

npm run typecheck:core                                                            # clean
npx eslint <touched files>                                                        # 0 new errors (9 pre-existing in route.ts)
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/integration/model-catalog-responsiveness-9199.test.ts  # 2/2
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/integration/provider-journey.contract.test.ts          # 14 tests / 0 fail
```

title: fix(combos): clear LKGP pins when a combo is deleted
body:
Closes #12326.

## Problem

`deleteCombo()` deleted the `combos` row but left the combo's LKGP pins in `key_value`. Pins are keyed by `${comboName}:${modelId}`, so once the combo is gone those rows become unreachable:

- the combo itself 404s, so no API or UI path addresses them
- `clearLKGP()` needs a `modelId` the caller no longer knows
- `clearAllLKGP()` wipes the namespace for *every* combo, which is not a targeted cleanup

On an instance with 26 live combos the `lkgp` namespace held 54 rows — 52 for live combos plus 2 orphans from a combo deleted earlier that day. Roughly 2 rows leak per deleted combo, so the table grows without bound for anyone who creates and deletes combos regularly.

## Fix

Provider-connection deletion already handles this via `deleteLKGPByConnectionIds()` (#8887), and `providers/deletion.ts` wraps it in try/catch so cleanup failures never block the delete. This applies the same pattern to combo deletion:

- **`deleteLKGPByComboName(comboName)`** in `settings/lkgp.ts` — deletes every pin under the `${comboName}:` prefix and calls `invalidateCachedLKGP()` for each, so a stale pin cannot be served from the 5s read cache for the rest of its TTL.
- **`deleteCombo()`** resolves the combo name before deleting the row, then clears its pins inside try/catch — a cleanup failure is logged, never fatal to the delete.

The `:` delimiter in the prefix keeps sibling combos safe (`prod` does not match `prod-canary`), and `LIKE` wildcards in combo names are escaped so a name like `temp_a` cannot match `tempXa`.

## Tests

New `tests/unit/combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup-12326.test.ts`, structured after the #8887 suite:

| Test | Covers |
|---|---|
| deleting a combo removes its LKGP pins | core fix, survivor pins untouched |
| invalidates warmed read-cache entries | the `invalidateCachedLKGP()` path |
| prefix-sharing sibling keeps its pins | `prod` vs `prod-canary` |
| `LIKE` wildcards do not widen cleanup | `temp_a` vs `tempXa` |
| unknown combo id leaves state untouched | early-return branch |
| combo without pins deletes cleanly | no-op path |

Verified the tests actually exercise the fix — with the cleanup block removed, 4 of 6 fail; with it restored, all 6 pass.

```
$ npx tsx --test tests/unit/combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup-12326.test.ts
# tests 6
# pass 6
# fail 0
```

No regressions in the existing LKGP suites:

```
$ npx tsx --test tests/unit/delete-provider-connection-invalidates-lkgp-8887.test.ts \
    tests/unit/lkgp-enabled-context-11181.test.ts \
    tests/unit/lkgp-stale-pin-exhaustion-11911.test.ts \
    tests/unit/combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup-12326.test.ts
# tests 18
# pass 18
# fail 0
```

`eslint` and `prettier --check` are clean on the touched files; `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in them (the repo's existing baseline errors are unrelated and untouched).

## Notes

- Changelog fragment added at `changelog.d/fixes/12330-combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup.md`.
- No behaviour change for combos that are never deleted; the new query only runs on the delete path.

title: fix(antigravity): surface image quotas in Provider Limits
body:
## Summary

- keep Antigravity image-only models excluded from chat discovery
- add a quota-specific visibility predicate for user-facing image quota buckets
- use that predicate when parsing both `fetchAvailableModels` and `retrieveUserQuota`
- add regression coverage proving `gemini-3.1-flash-image` is visible in Provider Limits while TTS/tab buckets remain hidden

## Problem

Antigravity quota parsing currently reuses `isDiscoverableAntigravityModelId()`. That predicate is intentionally chat-specific and excludes `gemini-3.1-flash-image`, so Google can return a valid image quota bucket from `retrieveUserQuota` / `fetchAvailableModels` and OmniRoute silently drops it before the Provider Limits UI sees it.

The image model should remain absent from the chat catalog, but its quota is user-facing because the model is callable through `/v1/images/generations`.

## Implementation

Introduce `isUserVisibleAntigravityQuotaModelId()` as a separate concern from chat discovery. It accepts normal discoverable chat models plus the known user-facing Antigravity image quota IDs, while continuing to reject TTS, tab-completion, retired, and other non-chat buckets.

`getAntigravityUsage()` now uses this quota predicate in both quota passes, including the `retrieveUserQuota`-only path.

## Related work

#9231 already fixed OAuth refresh / quota-aware credential selection and 401 account rotation for the image-generation route. This PR does not duplicate that work; it only fixes quota visibility in Provider Limits.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- regression test added for live `retrieveUserQuota` precedence (`25%` image quota) and non-chat filtering

title: fix(gemini): preserve response-schema nullability across union flattening
body:
## Summary

- `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` flattens every union spelling of "nullable" before a schema reaches Gemini: `flattenTypeArrays` turns `["string","null"]` into `"string"`, and `flattenAnyOfOneOf` drops the `{"type":"null"}` branch. That is correct for **tool parameters** and wrong for **response schemas**, where the union is the only thing telling the model that "nothing" is a legal answer. Stripped of it, a model with nothing to say returns the *string* `"null"` — or fabricates a value (live repro in #12308: an empty `{}` payload produced a fully-adjectived invented product). Pydantic emits the `anyOf` spelling for `Optional[str]`, so the fabricating path is the common one for Python consumers.
- A new `preserveNullable` walk runs as **Phase 1b**, before the Phase 2 flattening destroys the union: it records Gemini's sibling-key spelling, `nullable: true`, on any node whose `type` array contains `"null"` or whose `anyOf`/`oneOf` carries a `{"type":"null"}` branch.
- The key survives the rest of the pipeline for free: `nullable` is absent from `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS`, and `flattenAnyOfOneOf` merges the surviving branch with `Object.assign`, which cannot clobber a key the branch lacks. No existing pass changes.
- **Opt-in**: `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` gains `options: { preserveNullable?: boolean }` defaulting to off. Only the `responseSchema` call site in `openai-to-gemini.ts` passes it; the three tool-parameter call sites in `geminiToolsSanitizer.ts` keep today's behaviour exactly.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12308
- Related to #12307 (fix that one first — it corrupts the repro for this one)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: provider (Gemini/Antigravity translator path)
- [x] Focused tests from the golden path (commands below)
- [ ] `npm run lint` — targeted `npx eslint` run on the three touched files instead; full lint left to CI
      (every reported error reproduces identically on the untouched `release/v3.8.51` base — pre-existing, none introduced by this diff; the new/changed files themselves lint clean)
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (branched from `release/v3.8.51` HEAD `d920e64`)
- [x] Production-code changes include a new automated test in this PR

Commands run locally:

```bash
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/12308-gemini-response-schema-nullable.test.ts
npx eslint open-sse/translator/helpers/geminiHelper.ts \
  open-sse/translator/request/openai-to-gemini.ts \
  tests/unit/12308-gemini-response-schema-nullable.test.ts
```

Verified end-to-end against a live gateway carrying this change (unique nonce per request so nothing was served from cache):

```
type: ["string","null"]        -> {"value": null}     upstream 1685ms
anyOf: [{string},{null}]       -> {"value": null}     upstream 1697ms
oneOf: [{string},{null}]       -> {"value": null}     upstream 1674ms
anyOf: [{string},{number}]     -> {"value": "null"}   upstream 2242ms   <- negative control: no null branch, nothing marked
```

A/B on the same gateway, same prompts: with the fix, 5/5 real JSON nulls; without it, the string `"null"` and two fabricated descriptions.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/12308-gemini-response-schema-nullable.test.ts` (new): all three union spellings survive as `nullable: true`; nested fields are marked; a union **without** a null branch is left untouched; a caller-supplied `nullable: true` passes through; **the default (tool-parameter) call is byte-unchanged**; and a guard pins `nullable` out of `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` so a future keyword-list edit cannot silently kill the fix.

## Coverage Notes

- `geminiHelper.ts`: the new walk + options parameter are covered by all eight tests, including the negative control and the default-path test.
- `openai-to-gemini.ts`: a one-argument change at the `responseSchema` call site; visible in the diff, exercised by the live verification above. (Importing that module in a unit test drags in the executor/registry graph, so the call-site is deliberately not unit-tested — the helper-level flag semantics are.)

## Reviewer Notes

- **Tool-calling behaviour is deliberately untouched.** Flattening to a concrete type is correct for `functionDeclarations.parameters` (and `VALIDATED` mode depends on today's shapes); the flag exists so the fix cannot leak there. The default-path test locks this.
- Known limitation, pre-existing: `hasNullBranch` matches `type === "null"` exactly, mirroring the filter `flattenAnyOfOneOf` already uses — a branch written as `{"type": ["null"]}` is matched by neither. Rare; can be handled separately if it ever turns up.
- `claude-to-gemini.ts` imports this helper but never calls it (dead import, line 5); left alone here to keep the diff minimal.

title: fix(cache): fold the response output contract into the semantic cache signature
body:
## Summary

- The semantic-cache signature hashed only `{model, messages, temperature, top_p}`. Two temp=0 requests with identical messages but **different `response_format`** therefore shared a cache key, and the second was served the first's stored body under a 200 — a response that violates the schema it asked for. `tools`/`tool_choice` had the same exposure. (Live repro in #12307: a request for `{color, wheels}` was served a stored `{"value": "A vibrant red bicycle…"}`.)
- `generateSignature` now accepts an optional **output contract** — `response_format`, `text.format` (Responses API spelling), `tools`, `tool_choice`, collected by a new exported `outputContractOf(body)` — and folds it into the hashed payload **only when present**. Plain-chat signatures are byte-identical to before, so every existing plain-chat cache entry survives the upgrade; only structured-output/tool requests get new keys (their old entries age out within the 30-minute TTL).
- All three call sites pass it: the read path (`chatCore/semanticCache.ts`) and both write paths (`semanticCacheStore.ts`, `streamingSemanticCacheStore.ts`). Read/write key symmetry is preserved automatically because `bodyForCacheWrite` snapshots the same body object the read path hashed (the existing `#cache-signature-asymmetry` guard).

## Related Issues

- Closes #12307
- Related to #12308 (this cache defect corrupts the experiment used to investigate that one)

- [x] Change type: other — semantic cache (`src/lib` + chatCore decomposition modules)
- [x] Focused tests from the golden path (commands below)

Structured-output entries written by the old code become unreachable and expire via TTL; that is the point of the fix.

title: feat(memory): integrate turbovec vector store backend
body:
## Summary & Abstract

This pull request introduces a highly optimized, research-backed vector store tier into the OmniRoute memory system: **Turbovec** (based on Google Research's TurboQuant algorithm). 

Currently, OmniRoute's context retention relies on `sqlite-vec` (local) or Qdrant (remote/container). While `sqlite-vec` is highly portable, embedding heavy project files and long-lived agent memories locally scales linearly in RAM usage (Float32). To resolve this without forcing operators to host an external Qdrant container, this PR natively bridges Turbovec into the V8 runtime via N-API.

## Architectural Changes & Implementation Details

### 1. Zero-Overhead Native Rust Bridge (`packages/turbovec-node`)
- Scaffolded a zero-overhead Node API (N-API) binding mapping the Node.js execution cycle directly to the Rust `turbovec` crate.
- By binding `IdMapIndex` into JS/TS via `@node-rs/helper`, we allow Node.js to directly dispatch vector operations to underlying processor SIMD intrinsics (NEON on ARM; AVX-512/VNNI on x86) entirely bypassing V8 Garbage Collection latency.

### 2. State Mapping & Synchronization (`src/lib/memory/store.ts`)
- **Deterministic ID Mapping:** Turbovec requires `u64` numeric stable IDs. We structurally mapped SQLite's implicit integer `rowid` (`id` -> `BIGINT rowid`) to map directly to the Turbovec engine.
- Parallelized memory block upserts `upsertTurbovecPoint` and removals `deleteTurbovecPoint`. Data is natively synchronized incrementally to disk (`.tvim` format), ensuring crash safety without continuous block rebuilds.

### 3. Retrieval Engine Integration (`src/lib/memory/retrieval.ts`)
- Substituted the semantic retrieval execution loop to actively resolve queries using Turbovec when the engine is toggled. 
- Integrated the L2-distance / inner-product scoring output from the SIMD module into OmniRoute's standard RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) hybrid pipeline, guaranteeing that FTS5 keyword hits combine perfectly with Turbovec's dense vector ranks.

### 4. Policy Configuration & Schema Expansion (`src/shared/schemas/memory.ts`)
- Extended the `z.enum` bounds structurally for `vectorStore` arrays (`sqlite-vec`, `qdrant`, `turbovec`, `auto`), validating strict type compliance for the UI Engine tab (`MemoryEngineStatusSchema`) and API configuration.

## Projected Achievements (Performance Gains)

Integrating this architecture immediately unlocks several aggressive thresholds for OmniRoute installations:

1. **Extreme Memory Compression (16x RAM Saving):** 
   TurboQuant forces deterministic statistical distribution across hyperspheres, mapping float32 vectors into 4-bit and 2-bit spaces natively. A theoretical corpus of 10M embeddings compresses from ~31 GB down to ~3 GB without accuracy destruction. Resolves Agent `FATAL ERROR` memory limitations out-of-the-box.
2. **Sub-millisecond Search (Zero Network Latency):** 
   Qdrant imposes 15ms-60ms network overhead per recall stage. Turbovec executes purely in-memory via the N-API bounds (sub-1ms execution paths), accelerating contextual injections for auto-combo routers.
3. **Training-Free Online Ingest:**
   Unlike FAISS PQ setups that require explicit batch training or rebuilding as history scales, the implemented `IdMapIndex` operates completely on edge and supports un-batched `addWithIds()` synchronously at near O(1) ingestion times.

## Validation & Reviews

- **Opt-in Only:** The default configuration aggressively maintains fallback bounds. Turbovec requires explicit Opt-in over `sqlite-vec`, avoiding breaking changes for ongoing instances.
- **Data Integrity:** Testing confirms that FFI execution catches errors properly via standard `log.warn(...)` without halting the core Next.js SSE streams.
- Contains no API overrides; relies on standard REST endpoints mapping directly exactly as implemented for Qdrant. 

---
_Ref: Based on "TurboQuant: Online Vector Quantization with Near-optimal Distortion Rate" (ICLR 2026)._

title: fix(sse): classify "N API calls / month" 429 text as quota_exhausted
body:
### Problem

`QUOTA_PATTERNS` in `src/shared/utils/classify429.ts` recognizes `monthly ... limit`, `monthly ... quota` and `per month ... limit`, but not the **reversed phrase order** providers actually use in trial-key messages.

Cohere's trial-key 429 reads:

```
You are using a Trial key, which is limited to 1000 API calls / month.
```

None of the existing patterns match that, so `classify429()` returns `rate_limit` instead of `quota_exhausted`. The caller then applies the generic short transient backoff to an allowance that will not reset until the next billing cycle, and the same key is retried every few seconds for the rest of the month.

### Evidence

Measured on a production instance over 24h against two Cohere trial connections: **481 of 752** 429s carried this exact text, and every one was treated as a short transient rate limit. The connections were never cooled for a meaningful window, so traffic kept being dispatched to a provider with no remaining monthly quota.

### Fix

Three additional patterns covering the reversed order and the `N calls / month` / `N requests/month` spellings:

```ts
/(?:api\s+)?calls?\s*\/\s*month/i,
/requests?\s*\/\s*month/i,
/limited\s+to\s+[\d,]+.*(?:calls?|requests?).*per\s+month/i,
```

They are deliberately narrow — each requires an explicit `month` token adjacent to a call/request noun — so ordinary per-minute or per-day rate-limit text is unaffected.

### Tests

Added `monthly call allowances classify as quota_exhausted regardless of phrase order`, covering both orders plus the verbatim Cohere string.

Verified TDD on this branch:

- **Before the fix** the new test fails: `Limited to 1000 API calls per month` → `actual: 'rate_limit', expected: 'quota_exhausted'`.
- **After the fix** `tests/unit/classify429.test.ts` is 31/31.

No regressions in the neighbouring quota/classification suites:

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `classify429` | 31/31 |
| `circuit-breaker-failure-kind` | 12/12 |
| `antigravity-429-quota-tdd` | 5/5 |
| `antigravity-429-quota-cooldown` | 13/13 |
| `cloudflare-ai-neuron-exhaustion-6980` | 11/11 |
| `egress-ip-lock-10880` | 17/17 |

Prettier clean on both changed files.

### Notes

Branched from `origin/release/v3.8.51` and targets that branch. No open `base-red` issue and no active `release-freeze` at the time of cutting.

The changelog fragment is added in a follow-up commit on this branch once the PR number is known, per `changelog.d/README.md`.

title: fix(resilience): clear the combo LKGP pin only when it names the failed target
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #12013 (thanks @HouMinXi — the clearing itself is right, this only narrows *which* pin gets cleared).

#12013 clears the persisted LKGP pin from 13 call sites so a dead provider stops being re-pinned. None of them look at **which provider the pin names**, and the combo-level pin records whichever provider last *succeeded* — not necessarily the one failing now.

Under `lkgp` this is harmless: `applyStrategyOrdering` hoists the pinned target to index 0, so the pinned provider is always the first thing tried, and by the time anything else fails the pin either already refreshed or legitimately went stale.

Under **`auto` it is not**. `resolveAutoStrategy` reads the pin into `lastKnownGoodProvider` and feeds it to candidate *scoring* rather than hoisting it, so the pinned provider is not necessarily tried first. Skipping an unrelated target — a connection cooldown, a quota cutoff, an unavailable model — then discards a preference for a provider that never failed.

Measured on `63e4afa32`, same combo and same skip, only the strategy differing:

```
strategy=lkgp   pin after: {"provider":"felo"}   ← survives (felo hoisted first, succeeds)
strategy=auto   pin after: null                  ← destroyed
strategy=round-robin  pin after: null
```

In all three, `felo` is healthy and returns 200; the target that gets skipped is `opencode`.

This clears the combo-level pin only when it names the failed target's provider, and — when both sides carry one — its connection, so a sibling connection failing doesn't invalidate the pinned one. The target-scoped `executionKey` pin is still cleared unconditionally; that one is unambiguously about the target that just failed.

`failed` is optional, so a caller without a target in scope keeps the previous unconditional behaviour.

## Related Issues

- Refs #11911 (fixed by #12013; this narrows the clearing introduced there)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: routing (combo resilience)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint` — 21 problems on `open-sse/services/combo.ts`, **identical count on the base**; this adds none
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (`63e4afa32`); focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

The new test failed on `63e4afa32` before the fix.

The three tests #12013 added are the guard against over-narrowing, and they're what makes this safe — they pin the *same* provider that gets skipped, so they must keep passing. Mutation results:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| always clear (the pre-fix behaviour) | 1 fail — the new test |
| never clear the combo-level pin | 3 fail — all of #12013's tests |

So the guard can be neither too loose nor too tight without something going red.

```
tests/unit/lkgp-stale-pin-exhaustion-11911.test.ts
tests/unit/lkgp-enabled-context-11181.test.ts
tests/unit/delete-provider-connection-invalidates-lkgp-8887.test.ts
tests/unit/combo-stream-readiness-fallback.test.ts
tests/unit/combo/*.test.ts (12)
→ 139 tests, 139 pass, 0 fail
```

`npx tsc --noEmit` reports 0 errors for the touched files on the base and 0 with this change.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/lkgp-stale-pin-exhaustion-11911.test.ts` — 1 added: under `auto`, a pin naming healthy `felo` survives `opencode` being skipped. Added to #12013's own file so the LKGP behaviour stays described in one place.

## Coverage Notes

`open-sse/services/combo.ts` is the only production file changed, and both sides of the new branch are covered — the pin naming the failed provider (#12013's three tests) and naming a different one (the new test). Coverage does not move down in any touched file.

## Reviewer Notes

- The 13 call sites all now pass `target`, which they already had in scope; the change at each is one argument.
- Worth a second opinion on the connection-matching rule: I treat a pin as stale when the provider matches and *either* side lacks a `connectionId`. That deliberately errs toward clearing, so it stays closer to #12013's behaviour where the data is ambiguous.
- I reviewed the earlier #11914 and raised this same point there before it was closed; it didn't carry into #12013, and the call-site count went 2 → 13 in the meantime, which is what made it worth chasing down and measuring properly rather than leaving as a review comment.

title: fix(cli): setup-claude prints an absolute CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR hint (#11…
body:
Claude Code resolves CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR verbatim (`process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? join(homedir(), ".claude")`) and never expands `~`. The hint printed at the end of `omniroute setup-claude` used
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude/profiles/<name> claude`, which only works on a shell that expands the tilde itself. On PowerShell or cmd.exe the config dir does not resolve, settings.json is never read, the session starts with no ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, and Claude Code's `firstParty` provider falls back to api.anthropic.com — which rejects the OmniRoute key with a genuine Anthropic 401 `API key is invalid.`

`firstParty` is the provider kind, not a destination: it is what every non-Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/Mantle/gateway session is labelled, and its URL is resolved separately as ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL with api.anthropic.com only as the fallback. So the reported `dispatching to firstParty` line is expected output; the defect is the base URL never arriving, which our own printed hint caused.

- `formatManualLaunchHint()` emits the absolute profile directory in the host shell's syntax (PowerShell `$env:` form on win32, `VAR=value cmd` elsewhere), with a `<your OmniRoute key>` placeholder — never a real key. The command now prints it filled in with the first generated profile.
- `inheritedAnthropicKeyWarning()` warns when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is exported in the operator's shell: Claude Code sends it as x-api-key behind the "Detected a custom API key in your environment" prompt, which makes a base-URL-less session look configured until Anthropic answers 401. The warning never echoes the key back to the terminal.

Tests: 4 cases in tests/unit/cli/setup-claude.test.ts — the no-tilde invariant on both platforms, PowerShell syntax on win32, the key placeholder, and the warning's gate (unset / whitespace-only / set, and that it never echoes the key).

title: refactor(resilience): enforce passive lazy recovery for circuit breaker state transitions
body:
## Summary

Enforces passive lazy recovery for provider circuit breakers across read and evaluation paths (`canExecute()`, `getStatus()`, `execute()`, `getRetryAfterMs()`) when `resetTimeout` elapses. This replaces active background polling timers (`setInterval`) and removes module-level side effects on import, aligning implementation strictly with system architecture guidelines in `AGENTS.md` and repository submission governance rules. Also adds diagnostic response meta headers (`x-omniroute-target-attempts`, `x-omniroute-failure-reason`, `x-omniroute-fallback-attempts`) for observability.

## Related Issues

- None

## Validation

- [x] Change type: resilience / pipeline

  ```bash
  node --import tsx/esm --import ./open-sse/utils/setupPolyfill.ts --import ./tests/_setup/isolateDataDir.ts --test tests/unit/pipeline-optimizations-2026.test.ts
  ```

- [x] `npm run lint`

## Tests Added Or Updated

## Coverage Notes

## Reviewer Notes

title: feat(cli): add omniroute fcc-claude — FCC-style launcher with fallback chain
body:
## What

Adds `omniroute fcc-claude` — a Free-Claude-Code-style launcher built into OmniRoute.

## Why

FCC (free-claude-code) proved that a lightweight launcher with built-in fallback chains, streaming Anthropic Messages API support, and dual-upstream version tracking is valuable for coding-agent workflows. This ports those patterns natively into OmniRoute so users get the same ergonomics without running a separate FCC server.

## Changes

**New: `bin/cli/commands/fcc-claude.mjs`** (375 lines)
- `omniroute fcc-claude [options] [claude args...]` — launches Claude Code through OmniRoute with:
  - Built-in fallback chain: primary model fails → next model in chain automatically
  - `streamMessages()`: streaming Anthropic Messages client mirroring FCC's ProviderExecutor
  - `--test <prompt>`: non-interactive stream test mode
  - `--check-updates`: dual-upstream version tracking (OmniRoute health API + FCC GitHub)
  - `--models "a,b,c"`: inline fallback chain override
- Reuses `buildClaudeEnv` and `resolveLaunchTarget` from `launch.mjs` (no duplication)
- Supports both local (`localhost:20128`) and remote (`https://omni.paibao.ai`) OmniRoute instances

**Modified: `bin/cli/commands/registry.mjs`**
- +1 import, +1 register call

**New: `tests/unit/cli/fcc-claude.test.ts`** (208 lines, 12 tests)
- `loadFallbackChain`: defaults / opts override / file read
- `buildClaudeEnv` reuse: strips ANTHROPIC_* / sentinel token
- `streamMessages`: happy path / fallback transition / all-fail / header passthrough
- `fetchUpstreamVersions`: cache / graceful degradation

## E2E Verified

| Target | Model resolved | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `localhost:20128` | `gpt-4o-2024-11-20` | ✓ cost=0 |
| `omni.paibao.ai` | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` | ✓ cost=0 |
| fallback: nonexistent → `auto/best-chat` | succeeds | ✓ |

## Usage

```bash
# Local
omniroute fcc-claude
omniroute fcc-claude -- "帮我写个 bug"

# Remote
omniroute fcc-claude --remote https://omni.paibao.ai

# Custom fallback chain
omniroute fcc-claude --models "auto/pro-coding,auto/best-coding,auto/offline"

# Non-interactive test
omniroute fcc-claude --test "hello" --remote https://omni.paibao.ai

# Version check
omniroute fcc-claude --check-updates
```

title: security(runtime): harden TLS provenance, lifecycle, and public error boundaries
body:
## Summary

This draft hardens the frozen `release/v3.8.50` line around the native
`tls-client-node` supply chain, runtime lifecycle, and public error/log boundaries. It is
independent of other PRs, but it **does change provider executors and validation behavior**;
the previous narrower scope statement is intentionally superseded.

| Area | What changed | Evidence | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native dependency provenance | Pins `tls-client-node@0.2.0`, records the exact wrapper/upstream licenses and NOTICE, and pins all six supported v1.15.1 native assets to official SHA-256 digests | License/provenance and tamper regressions; manifest/source hash checks | PASS for recorded provenance and policy |
| Build and packaging policy | Verifies the native binary before runtime/build copies and carries `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` through npm, standalone, Docker, and Electron assembly paths | Build/pack policy tests, MJS syntax checks, and exact-head production build/artifact evidence below | Source/policy and exact-head production build PASS; real pack, Docker, and Electron artifacts remain HOLD |
| Runtime lifecycle and install lock | Adds bounded lifecycle coordination, safe retries, handle/inode/device/nonce lock ownership, cross-process coverage, and fail-closed cleanup | TLS serial matrix `47/47`, including 100 callers and cross-process contention | PASS on local filesystems |
| Error boundary | Extracts a canonical sanitizer for credentials, stacks, recognized filesystem paths, hostile Proxies, Unicode/serialized separators, and public identifiers | Canonical matrix `121/121`; runtime/spec review CLEAR | PASS |
| Provider consumers | Hardens ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Perplexity, Notion, LM Arena, moderation, OCR, and provider validation without exposing raw upstream errors | Provider-specific matrices listed below | PASS within tested boundaries |
| LM Arena public failures | Projects HTTP, network, TLS, upstream-event, and stream-transport failures through a closed local union; rejects raw upstream bodies/stacks/causes and accepts only public error statuses `400..599` | Iteration-4 RED `53/55` -> GREEN `55/55`; final Arena matrix `124/124`; direct CodeQL #968 fixed | PASS locally and in final CodeQL analysis |
| Perplexity streaming | Preserves early quota/upstream HTTP status through a bounded preflight, replays normal content without duplication, and releases readers/iterators | `54/54` | PASS with late-error limit below |
| Logs and usage | Sanitizes call-log, pipeline, lifecycle, console, and request payload fields while preserving internal classification | Semaphore SSE+JSON regression; request-log regressions | PASS |
| Documentation | Corrects privacy/local-processing language and documents the exact sanitizer boundary | Docs gates | PASS |
| Contributor ranking | No new ranking rewrite was needed: the `.50` base already contains a newer census than the supplied dossier snapshot | README: 5,911 merged PR census, 535 distinct external contributors, and 639 normalized human Git identities | Already present in base |

## Exact branch boundary

- Base: `091589089cd134a94df9f6cdab9ba562b2cefd18` (`release/v3.8.50`).
- Candidate: `29dc5427b6abd5a4ff5198759f8cfc2d500ce1aa`.
- Physical scope: **97 paths** = 74 modified + 23 added, +18,409 / -1,941 against the exact base.
- Commit count: 6 commits after the exact base.
- Production/runtime scope: 32 paths under `open-sse/` or `src/`; there are no production
  changes under `electron/` or `bin/`.
- This PR does not depend on #11753. That draft is an alternative `wreq-js` migration for
  `release/v3.8.51`; this PR deliberately keeps the exact `.50` base and hardens the dependency
  shipped there.
- The final scope intentionally uses the broader **TLS + public error boundary hardening**
  boundary. It therefore includes the five Moderation/OCR helper-and-test paths instead of
  presenting them as TLS-only work; the title, summary table, and changelog all name that expansion.

## Runtime and security changes

### Native dependency and lifecycle

- Verify the selected native asset against the checked-in platform manifest before loading or
  copying it.
- Reject version drift, digest mismatch, symlink/path substitution, and unsafe lock ownership.
- Keep the exclusive install-lock handle open for the operation and verify nonce plus inode/device
  identity before cleanup, so an older owner does not delete a newer owner's lock.
- Coordinate shared-client start/stop, retries, stream leases, timeout/abort settlement, and cleanup
  without retaining native stack/cause data.
- Project TLS stream error names through a closed allowlist:
  `Error`, `AbortError`, `TimeoutError`, `BodyTimeoutError`, `TlsClientHangError`, and
  `NativeTlsError`; every other, hostile, or credential-shaped value falls back to `Error`.

### Public errors and persistent logs

- Route HTTP, JSON, SSE, executor, validation, moderation, OCR, and call-log messages through the
  canonical error sanitizer.
- Defensively snapshot hostile rejection fields with protected single reads; accessors and
  `getPrototypeOf` traps fail closed.
- Redact strong tokens, labeled credentials, stack frames, recognized POSIX/Windows/UNC/file-URL
  paths, raw and serialized line separators, and sensitive nested request-log payloads.
- Preserve safe status codes, `Retry-After`, SSE framing, public error codes, and internal cooldown /
  usage classification.
- Sanitize the semaphore-capacity message before it reaches SSE, JSON, call-log, pipeline, or
  lifecycle events while preserving HTTP `429` and `SEMAPHORE_TIMEOUT`.

### Provider-specific behavior

- Perplexity: bounded preflight (up to 32 semantic chunks or 250 ms) promotes early quota/upstream
  failures before SSE headers commit, replays normal thinking/content once, and closes readers and
  iterators.
- Grok: sanitizes chunk, reader, fetch, and TLS failures in streaming and non-streaming paths.
- LM Arena: maps every public failure through a closed discriminated union and
  `buildErrorBody()`. Non-2xx TLS bodies are never reflected; network/TLS exceptions, upstream SSE
  errors, and stream-reader failures become fresh locally constructed errors without upstream
  `cause` or stack. Only integer status codes in the error range `400..599` survive projection;
  success/redirect, invalid, coercive, and hostile values fall back to `502`.
- ChatGPT/Claude/Notion: protect TLS and provider-specific error classification against hostile
  Proxies and sanitize transport metadata.
- Provider validation: fail closed when proxy-fallback metadata or TLS/header metadata is hostile;
  the route logs only the canonical sanitized message and imports the specific DB modules rather
  than the restricted barrel.

## Legal and provenance disposition

Primary sources:

- [`fatihkabakk/tls-client-node@v0.2.0` LICENSE](https://github.com/fatihkabakk/tls-client-node/blob/v0.2.0/LICENSE) — SHA-256 `086c687026ff693ad76589dda1af12304a3ff33fc5f15030035ed62ef6a6d6eb`;
- [`fatihkabakk/tls-client-node@v0.2.0` NOTICE](https://github.com/fatihkabakk/tls-client-node/blob/v0.2.0/NOTICE) — SHA-256 `80e5a526273788f2ace0164ec131daac697c54084add90855afdd03f5fadd3d3`;
- [`bogdanfinn/tls-client@v1.15.1` LICENSE](https://github.com/bogdanfinn/tls-client/blob/v1.15.1/LICENSE) — SHA-256 `7dab9a4dd66987fbe576d53c1ee047c193725df6f4fac67de315a127417fd151`;
- [`bogdanfinn/tls-client@v1.15.1` release](https://github.com/bogdanfinn/tls-client/releases/tag/v1.15.1) — source of the six asset digests.

The Commons Clause makes `tls-client-node` source-available and commercially restrictive.
Distributing notices does **not** grant a right to sell a product or service covered by that
restriction. The exception remains medium risk and temporary, owned by `@diegosouzapw`, with review
due `2026-09-30` / `v3.9.0`. Legal review, separate permission, or replacement with a permissive
transport is still required before commercial deployment. This PR records obligations and reduces
provenance risk; it is not legal advice and does not cure the restriction.

Current shared transport consumers: `chatgpt-web`, `claude-web`, `perplexity-web`, `grok-web`,
`notion-web`, and `lmarena`.

## TDD and focused verification

RED -> GREEN was captured for the native manifest/license/NOTICE contract, tampered binaries,
runtime version drift, unsafe install-lock replacement, lifecycle contention, hostile
`instanceof`/properties/coercion, credential-shaped `Error.name`, Perplexity early quota and replay,
public error/log sinks, provider validation fallback metadata, semaphore call-log persistence, the
CodeQL polynomial data-URL regex, omitted-media-type data URLs, LM Arena upstream stack/body
reflection, closed stream-transport projection, and rejection of public `2xx`/`3xx` statuses.

Focused results on the final candidate:

| Matrix | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| LM Arena iteration-4 status regressions | RED `53/55`, then GREEN `55/55` |
| Arena / LM Arena serial aggregate | `124/124 PASS` |
| TLS lifecycle/download/install-lock/timeout, serial | `47/47 PASS` |
| Perplexity | `54/54 PASS` |
| Grok | `78/78 PASS` |
| Canonical sanitizer / ChatCore helpers | `121/121 PASS` |
| Provider-validation error sanitizer | `7/7 PASS` |
| Final TLS/header validation slice | `7/7 PASS` |
| Moderation + OCR | `24/24 PASS` |
| Notion | `41/41 PASS` |
| Semaphore SSE + JSON + fresh call-log/pipeline | `1/1 PASS` |
| CodeQL data-URL scanner + canonical sanitizer regression slice | `85/85 PASS` |

The TLS parallel aggregate produced `46/47 LOAD-RED` because the 100-caller stress exceeded its
75-second limit under CPU contention; the same case passed alone in 48.3 seconds and in the serial
`47/47` matrix. A later broad ChatCore slice was `4/11 INFRA-RED`: seven cases were rejected by the
real resource-pressure guard while the cgroup was at 96.7%+ usage; the changed case passed alone.
Neither result is represented as a full-suite PASS.

## Repository gates

PASS on exact candidate `29dc5427b6abd5a4ff5198759f8cfc2d500ce1aa`:

- `npm run typecheck:core`;
- `npm run check:cycles`;
- scoped ESLint with the repository suppressions file (0 errors);
- Prettier on the final changed implementation/test paths;
- `git diff --check`;
- `npm run check:error-helper`;
- `npm run test:vitest -- --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism`: the first run reached `404/405`
  because one `auto/glm` case timed out; that isolated slice then passed `11/11`, and the clean retry
  completed `405/405`.

PASS recorded earlier in the branch and unaffected by the final LM Arena-only commits:

- MJS syntax (`node --check`, 8/8);
- `npm run check:file-size` (4,408 production and 5,086 test files checked);
- `npm run check:secrets -- --ratchet` (0 findings);
- `npm run check:any-budget:t11`;
- `npm run check:tracked-artifacts`;
- `npm run check:docs-all` and `npm run check:docs-counts` (only the two existing soft
  executor-count notices);
- `npm run check:route-validation:t06`;
- `npm run check:build-scope`.

Exact-head full-suite and artifact evidence:

- **PASS:** full `npm run test:vitest:ui -- --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism` on `29dc5427` —
  285/285 files and `1,816/1,816` tests in 1,417.66s, with an isolated temporary `DATA_DIR`.
- **PASS:** remote `Fast Production Build` / `npm run build:release` on `29dc5427` in 18m21s;
  the `omniroute-build` artifact was uploaded (4,996,056,168 bytes).
- **PASS:** DAST smoke in 8m34s, Semgrep in 3m07s, and Semgrep Cloud on `29dc5427`.
- **PASS:** Change Classification in 49s. Seven Quality Gates fast-path jobs were **SKIPPED** by
  the classifier and are not counted as PASS.
- **PASS:** remote CodeQL JavaScript/TypeScript on `29dc5427` in 48m30s; Actions, C/C++, Python,
  and the Advanced Security aggregate also passed.
- **FIXED:** direct alert #967 (`js/polynomial-redos`), with no dismissal or suppression. The
  final PR ref has no open code-scanning alert.
- **FIXED:** direct alert #968 (`js/stack-trace-exposure`), with no dismissal or suppression. Its
  stored most-recent instance changed from `open` to `fixed` after the final analysis.

## Bounded CodeQL remediation history

| Iteration | Candidate | Observation | Action / result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `b40a9fc3` | Language analyses passed, but the outer Advanced Security verdict failed with #967 `js/polynomial-redos` and #968 `js/stack-trace-exposure` | Started bounded remediation; no alert was dismissed or suppressed |
| 2 | `e5d1bbc9` | The deterministic data-URL scanner fixed direct alert #967. Build, DAST, Semgrep, all CodeQL language jobs, and the outer aggregator passed, but direct alert #968 remained open | Demonstrated that the green aggregate alone was insufficient; continued from the direct alert |
| 3 | `d66748406f` | Closed LM Arena's public-failure union and routed stream transport through the canonical error builder; static review still found that projected HTTP status accepted public `2xx`/`3xx` values | Added a narrower regression instead of declaring completion |
| 4 | `29dc5427` | Normalizes public LM Arena statuses to integer `400..599` and rejects success/redirect, invalid, coercive, and hostile values | TDD RED `53/55` -> GREEN `55/55`; Arena matrix `124/124`; all CodeQL language jobs and the aggregate PASS; direct #967/#968 FIXED |

Iteration-1 remote evidence on `b40a9fc3` included `Fast Production Build` PASS in 18m56s, DAST
PASS in 8m39s, Semgrep and Semgrep Cloud PASS, and all four CodeQL language jobs PASS. Iteration-2
remote evidence on `e5d1bbc9` included `Fast Production Build` PASS in 19m01s, DAST/Semgrep PASS,
all CodeQL language jobs PASS, and the outer aggregator PASS. Quality Gates fast-path jobs skipped
by workflow classification are never counted as PASS.

## Exact-base / non-candidate reds

- `npm run typecheck:noimplicit:core` reports 36 errors only in unchanged
  `open-sse/translator/response/openai-responses/pureHelpers.ts`; the file is byte-identical to the
  exact base, so this is `BASE-RED`.
- `docs/i18n/it/README.md`, `docs/i18n/tr/README.md`, and
  `tests/unit/grok-web.test.ts` are Prettier-red on both the candidate and exact base; no broad
  reformat is included here.
- The live `npm run check:changelog-integrity` compares this frozen `.50` tree with the newer
  `origin/release/v3.8.51` and reports ten `.51` bullets as missing. `CHANGELOG.md` on this candidate
  is byte-identical to exact base `091589...`; only the owned changelog fragment is added, so this is
  branch drift / `BASE-RED`, not a candidate regression.
- The Claude native test reaches its material assertions and then terminates in the same `koffi`
  fatal on the candidate and exact base: `BASE-RED`.
- `npm run check:circular-deps` invokes the shell shim `node_modules/.bin/dpdm` through Node and
  currently fails before graph analysis; this is distinct from the passing `npm run check:cycles`
  result above and is not called a candidate PASS.
- `npm run check:open-sse-typecheck` reports a new-baseline mismatch only in unchanged
  `src/app/api/v1/models/catalog.ts`; the relevant source/config blobs are identical to the exact
  base, so this remains `BASE-RED`, not a candidate PASS.

## HOLD / not claimed

- Full production dependency-license scan from a clean lockfile install: the shared `node_modules`
  is contaminated and cannot prove the exact dependency tree.
- Commercial authorization for the Commons Clause dependency.
- Real npm pack/boot artifact, Docker Node/Bun images, and Electron Linux/Windows/macOS artifacts.
- `npm run check:pack-policy` / its real `npm pack --dry-run` did not finish within more than ten
  minutes and was interrupted without a verdict.
- Artifact homologation/deployment.
- Full `npm run test:unit` and coverage.

These HOLDs keep the PR in draft. They are not presented as PASS and do not authorize merge,
release, or deployment.

## Known runtime boundaries

- Install-lock guarantees are for local filesystems; NFS/CIFS equivalence is not claimed.
- Node provides no atomic compare-and-unlink, so a minimal TOCTOU window remains despite the live
  handle, inode/device, and nonce checks.
- A native synchronous call cannot be preempted by JavaScript; process-exit cleanup is best effort.
- A never-settling native start/cleanup can retain a discarded lifecycle lease; there is no safe
  JavaScript TTL that can interrupt the native library.
- A Perplexity error after the bounded preflight and after SSE `200` is committed cannot be promoted
  to an HTTP `429/502`.

## Maintainer boundary

- Leave this PR open and draft.
- No merge or auto-merge.
- No tag, release, publish, deployment, or homologation action is part of this PR.

title: feat: Organizations multi-tenant layer + client-abort server resilience [defer to 3.8.51]
body:
## Summary

This PR bundles two improvements to OmniRoute:

### 1. Organizations (multi-tenant) layer
- Multi-user mode toggle, organization management, members, invitations, org-scoped combos/connections/quota.
- New dashboard section `Organizations` and API routes under `/api/v1/organizations/*`.
- Email verification for registration (P4).

### 2. Client-abort server resilience (bugfix)
- Prevents a client disconnect (`aborted` / `ECONNRESET` on the incoming socket) from crashing the dev/prod HTTP server via an unhandled `uncaughtException`.
- Adds `httpClientAbortGuard` (shared module + dev-server integration) that swallows client-abort errors while preserving genuine crash semantics.
- Applied to sibling `createServer` call sites: `apiBridgeServer`, `liveServer` (WS), `embedWsProxy`.
- Includes unit tests (`tests/unit/httpClientAbortGuard.test.mjs`, 8/8 passing).

### 3. i18n fix
- Adds missing translation keys (`auth.*`, `common.*`, `sidebar.*`, `cheaperInferenceSponsorBanner`) to `en.json` / `ru.json` to resolve `MISSING_MESSAGE` IntlError console spam on the `ru` locale.

## Test plan
- `node --test tests/unit/httpClientAbortGuard.test.mjs` > 8/8 passing.
- Manual: server survives browser client-aborts (bcache/HMR/WebSocket disconnect) without `uncaughtException: aborted`.

## Base branch
Targets `release/v3.8.50` (current active release branch).

title: feat(teams): add billing cost centers and soft shared budgets [defer to 3.8.51]
body:
## Summary

Adds Team **billing cost centers** and **soft shared budgets**, targeted at `release/v3.8.51`.

This head is a merge of the public candidate lineage (`1642794b7`) with LIVE `release/v3.8.51` (`e0ea3f92e`), so the branch is reconciled against the current release line rather than an older snapshot.

| | |
|---|---|
| Head | `6e842d89241251f715f10cd02d8950578c44765b` |
| Tree | `318133236c4c53568aa3e16c050cc9ad6943770f` |
| parent^1 (candidate lineage) | `1642794b7f3169cd074929cb7ed862227aa06167` |
| parent^2 (LIVE `release/v3.8.51`) | `e0ea3f92e1403351686cb783764ba3da6bbddd75` |

### Reconciliation with LIVE

Diff against the previously reviewed candidate tree is exactly **five files**:

| File | Relation to LIVE `e0ea3f92e` |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | blob-identical |
| `package-lock.json` | blob-identical |
| `electron/package.json` | blob-identical |
| `electron/package-lock.json` | blob-identical |
| `config/quality/eslint-suppressions.json` | intentionally **not** identical — both sides edited it |

The suppressions file is the only semantic merge. Its resulting keyset is exactly the intersection of the two sides (1368 → 1366): both sides' deletions are honoured, with no resurrected entries, no silent additions, and valid JSON.

### Migration placement

- The migration lands at slot **`164_team_cost_centers.sql`** — exactly one file, not renumbered.
- Canonical `163_radar_feed_cache_generated_at.sql` is **byte-identical to LIVE**; so are `src/lib/db/migrationRunner.ts` and `scripts/check/check-migration-numbering.mjs` (the numbering gate is not weakened by this branch).
- `RENAMED_MIGRATION_COMPATIBILITY` carries **153 / 154 / 155 / 161 / 163 → 164**, every mapping **name-locked** to `team_cost_centers`.

Because the applied-migrations table keys on `version TEXT PRIMARY KEY` and every lookup/update/delete matches on **version AND name**, a mapping cannot rehome a row belonging to a different migration name. Installs that already applied this migration at an earlier slot are rehomed to 164; the canonical 163 row is untouched.

### Gates re-run on this exact tree

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `check:migration-numbering` | exit **0** — 161 migrations, **0 duplicates** |
| Team invariant suite (repo's own `node:test` runner, 10 files) | **90/90 pass**, 0 fail |

### Note on the historical red `dast-smoke`

The `dast-smoke` failure recorded against the **previously published head** is **base-attributed, not candidate-owned**:

- That run's own `server.log` artifact shows the server never booted — 205 `sql-wasm.wasm` fatals, **0 migrations applied**, 0 SQLite-level errors, 0 team/billing references. The reported 500s are "nothing is serving", so candidate code never executed.
- Root cause is upstream issue **#11343**, opened **2h29m before** that run and closed the same day, traced to base commit `10276821cd` (#10952) — an ancestor of LIVE, not of this branch's changes.
- This reviewed tree's `next.config.mjs` is blob-identical to LIVE and carries the `OMNIROUTE_BETTER_SQLITE3_STUB` gating fix, which the previously published head lacked. This branch touches **zero packaging paths**.

Please don't read that historical red as a defect of this PR.

### Verified vs unverified

**Verified locally on this tree:** migration-numbering gate, Team invariant suite (90/90), migration placement and compatibility-map invariants, blob identity of the reconciled files against LIVE.

**Not verified — stated honestly:**

- Full Node unit suite was **not** run.
- Both backend-only builds **timed out** at the same Turbopack stage.
- Server start, Schemathesis, and promptfoo are **unverified locally**.
- **No claim** is made about `sql-wasm.wasm` behaviour or packaging output for this tree.

Kept as **Draft** pending maintainer direction.
